⚠️ KEPT DELIBERATELY BY UNDO_26 (Mission 8). Carrying the history across APPLY would need
proof that every snapshot belongs to the exact accepted revision the Main App now holds —
and the Main App rewrites what it receives (cut normalisation, trim offsets, meme
re-timing), so the accepted state is not provably the editor's last snapshot. Without that
proof, a Ctrl+Z after reopening could replay a pre-APPLY state over a newer accepted one.
Correctness beats deeper undo history; the Main App's own history (PROJSESSION) records the
APPLY as one step instead.

### GranularSpeedEditorWindow.AdoptParkedHistory — UNDO_25, UNDO_26, UNDO_24 (line 254)

UNDO_25 — THE HISTORY OUTLIVES THE WINDOW THAT MADE IT.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
**THE DEFECT THIS CLOSES.** A user spent ten minutes on speed ramps and zoom boxes,
closed the editor to look at the main timeline, reopened it, pressed Ctrl+Z — and nothing
happened, because `OnClosed` had called `ClearUndoHistory`.

⚠️ KEYED BY CLIP PATH, AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING. Restoring history into a DIFFERENT clip
would let a Ctrl+Z apply segment boundaries measured against another video's duration.
UNDO_26 adds the REVISION: the parked history also records the state its session opened on
and the state it closed on, and it is replayed only into an editor that opens on one of
those exact states (`GranularEditHistory.BelongsTo`). A different project using
the same file, or an APPLY / main-window edit since, opens on another state and the history
is dropped without hesitation.

⚠️ PROCESS-LIFETIME ONLY, DELIBERATELY. This survives closing the WINDOW, not closing the
APP: cross-restart history is the sidecar's job (`UndoSidecarStore`, UNDO_24).

⚠️ ONE SLOT, NOT A DICTIONARY. Holding history for every clip ever opened is an unbounded
leak in a process that also holds decoded video frames.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

UNDO_25 — parks the history on the way out, in place of throwing it away (see

### GranularSpeedEditorWindow._freezeArmed (line 126)

FREEZE_ARM — true when the playhead is BEHIND the freeze point and the hold is therefore
still owed. Set the moment the playhead is seen before the freeze, cleared the moment the
hold fires.

⚠️ THIS REPLACED A DISTANCE GUARD, AND THE DISTANCE GUARD IS WHY THE FREEZE PLAYED ONCE AND
THEN SOMETIMES NOT AGAIN. The old test was
`Math.Abs(currentAbsMs - _lastFreezeTriggerAbsMs) > 500`, with
`_lastFreezeTriggerAbsMs` set to the freeze point after firing. It was trying to say
"do not immediately re-fire the hold we just finished" — but what it actually asks is "is
the playhead more than half a second away from the freeze point", and on the SECOND pass the
playhead crosses that point again at a distance of ~0. So the guard, which cannot tell a
re-entry from an echo, silently suppressed the freeze. Whether it fired depended on how far
the tick happened to land past the mark: near it, suppressed; a slow frame that overshot by
more than 500ms, fired. Hence "sometimes".

Arming is the right question. "Have we approached the mark from before it since the last
time it fired?" has one answer, the same answer every pass, and it re-arms itself for free
on a rewind, a seek backwards or a replay.

1.5s hold on a 60s clip puts the two heads ~20px apart inside 52px of width and they cover
each other by more than half. For that case the vertical stagger is what makes them two

start head is then pure visual noise — it reads as a misaligned pair, which is exactly the
bug this note exists to prevent. Compare the two *clamped* lefts, not the raw lane X:
the clamp pins a head at the canvas edge, so raw separation lies at both ends of the ruler.

Every output moment of a 1.5s freeze maps to the SAME source instant, and
`SourceToOutput` of that instant is defined to already include the WHOLE hold. So while
the freeze plays, a derived caret sits pinned at the far edge of the hold: it leaps the
frozen seconds in one step at the moment the freeze begins and then does not move for 1.5
seconds. The ruler grew by the freeze — correctly, TIME_02 — but the caret refused to walk
across the space it added.

directly instead. Non-null ONLY while the caret is inside a held span; every path that moves

### GranularSpeedEditorWindow.DecorateFrozenSpan — TIME_02 (line 439)

FREEZE_VIS — MAKES A HELD SPAN LOOK HELD.

The thumbnail lane already stretched the frozen frame across the whole hold (TIME_02/F4),
which is literally what the exported file shows — and that is exactly why it was not
readable. A stretched frame looks like ordinary footage that happens to be slow, or like a
rendering glitch. Nothing said "time is stopped here".

Four cues, each doing a different job, because one alone is ambiguous:

  - A cool blue WASH — the same blue as the freeze block above it, so the
  two read as one object spanning both lanes rather than a marker and some odd footage.
  - Diagonal HATCHING — the universal "this region is not normal content"
  cue. It also survives where colour alone does not: over a blue-ish frame, over a blown-out
  white one, and for a colour-blind user.
  - Solid POSTS at both ends — the wash says "something here", the posts
  say exactly WHERE it starts and stops, which is the thing being asked of the timeline.
  - A centred ❄ LABEL with the duration, when there is room for it. Removes
  the last of the guesswork; suppressed on narrow spans rather than clipped to mush.

Everything added here is `IsHitTestVisible = false`. The upper lane runs its own pointer
pipeline for block move, edge resize and drag-to-create; a decoration that swallowed a press
would break editing over every freeze.

### GranularSpeedEditorWindow.CreateAsync — GRANPROBE_01, RECOVERY_03 (line 581)

Creates the Granular Speed Editor constrained to a trim region.
The editor will only show/seek between trimStartMs and trimEndMs.
Segments are stored in absolute video timestamps.

GRANPROBE_01 — THE SUPPORTED WAY TO OPEN THIS WINDOW.

Resolves the clip duration OFF the UI thread and only then constructs the window, so the
constructor keeps its "everything is final on exit" contract — which
TryRehydrateGranularRecovery (RECOVERY_03) and the whole deferred-close chain
(docs/05 §SYS-WINSTATE) depend on — without the dispatcher ever blocking.

The probe is bounded at 10 seconds here. MediaProber runs ffprobe through AsyncProcessRunner,
which carries its own 15-second timeout, registers the child with ChildProcessTracker and
terminates it through the graceful ladder while draining both pipes — so a probe that
overruns this wait cannot leave an orphaned ffprobe behind either.

A probe that fails or times out is NOT fatal: the window opens on the trim window the caller
supplied, exactly as it did when the old 500ms blocking wait expired. The difference is that
the UI stayed responsive while it happened.

### GranularSpeedEditorWindow.GranularSpeedEditorWindow — GRANPROBE_01 (line 652)

⚠️ GRANPROBE_01 — PREFER `CreateAsync`. This constructor no longer probes.

`preProbedDurationSec` is the clip length already resolved OFF the UI thread
by `CreateAsync`. Constructing this window directly with a zero
`trimEndMs` and no pre-probe now yields a zero-length timeline instead of
silently blocking the dispatcher — which is the correct trade, and why CreateAsync exists.

### GranularSpeedEditorWindow.SeekInternal — SEEKSTORM_01 (line 1232)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SEEKSTORM_01 — THE GATE BELOW IS TIME-BASED ON PURPOSE. DO NOT RE-COUPLE IT TO _isSeeking.

It used to read `if (_isSeeking && (now - _lastSeekTimestamp < 350))`. On a GPU/cuda path mpv
raises SeekCompleted 1–3ms after each seek, and that handler clears _isSeeking — so the first
half of the condition was false again before the next pointer-move arrived and the 350ms
window was NEVER consulted. The coalescer looked present and did nothing: every single
PointerMoved during a segment-edge drag issued a real absolute seek.

MEASURED (dev log 2026-09-11, mpv_debug_27808): one drag produced 310 seeks in 1.74s, 271 of
them ≤3ms apart, 78 in the final 200ms. Each seek forces a FULL mpv playback restart —
lavf seek, decoder re-init, WASAPI `Thread Reset`/`Thread Pause`. The render thread stops
draining, the UI thread blocks behind it, and the app freezes with mpv still spinning (the
app log dies while mpv_debug keeps growing — that asymmetry is the signature).

This is the same rule §42 Edge Case J already states for the zoom prime and DRAG_FIX already
enforced for the meme block: NOTHING that talks to mpv may run per pointer-move.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### GranularSpeedEditorWindow.EnsureSeekFlushTimer — SEEKSTORM_01 (line 1277)

GPU live zoom preview engine. Mirrors GranularSpeedBuilder's export math 1:1:
steal windows (>=0.5s available, capped at 1.0s, vs neighboring zooms only),
linear ramp progress, zVal = 1 + (targetZ - 1) * p with the view center lerping
from frame center to the zoom-box center. The equivalent visible source region
is applied via mpv `video-crop` ("WxH+X+Y"); mpv's own aspect-fit letterboxing
then matches the export's force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease + pad stage.
NOTE: near frame edges the export shows black padding where this preview clamps
the crop inside the frame — an accepted, minor visual difference.

### GranularSpeedEditorWindow.ClampToVideo — ZOOM_06 (line 4779)

Clamp a candidate box into the video rect, preserving aspect and floor.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
⚠️ ZOOM_06 — THE Math.Max ON EACH AXIS IS LOAD-BEARING. DO NOT "SIMPLIFY" IT AWAY.

This method used to call `Math.Clamp(r.X, vid.X, vid.Right - w)` directly, and that CRASHED
THE WHOLE APPLICATION:
    ArgumentException: '600.2810304449649' cannot be greater than 600.2810304449648
Math.Clamp throws when min > max, and here they differed by ONE UNIT IN THE LAST PLACE.

HOW TWO IDENTICAL NUMBERS DISAGREE. Drag the box wider than the area it is allowed to fill
and the first line pins `w` to exactly `vid.Width`. The maximum X is then `vid.Right - w`,
and `vid.Right` is itself stored as `vid.X + vid.Width`. In exact arithmetic
(vid.X + vid.Width) - vid.Width is vid.X. In binary floating point it can land one ulp
BELOW it — so min (vid.X) becomes greater than max, and Math.Clamp throws rather than
returning either. A pointer-move handler is the worst possible place for that: it fires on
every mouse movement, the throw escapes into Avalonia's input loop, and the process dies
mid-drag with the user's segment work unsaved.

THE SECOND CASE THIS ALSO FIXES: on a very small preview, or a low-resolution source in
portrait, the quality floor `minW` can legitimately exceed the usable width. Then
`vid.Right - w` is genuinely, largely below `vid.X` — not a rounding hair — and the old code
would have thrown just the same. Pinning to `vid.X` puts the oversized box at the left edge
of the usable area, which is the only sane answer.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### GranularSpeedEditorWindow.ZoomOutputWidthSource — ZOOM_01, UNITS_01 (line 4822)

ZOOM_01 — the width of the frame the VIEWER finally sees, IN SOURCE PIXELS.

It handed back `CoordinateConstants.PortraitW` (1080) in portrait — the width of the
FINISHED FILE. What the viewer actually sees is the surviving slice of the SOURCE, which is
720px on a 1920x1080 capture and 960px on a 2560x1440 one: `InternalW / scale`, the same
quantity `ZoomPreviewSimulator.PortraitSurvivingWidth` computes. Feeding an output width
into a source-pixel divisor inflated the minimum zoom box by exactly the ratio between them
(1080/720 = 1.5x), so the `MaxZoomUpscale` quality floor bit 1.5x too early and the real
ceiling was 5.33x, not the 8x this constant declares. It is also what produced the W=134
box in the drift report — the user drew smaller and the floor silently snapped it up.
Landscape was always correct, which is why it went unnoticed.

### GranularSpeedEditorWindow._frameLaneQueued — TIME_02 (line 5342)

TIME_02 / F4 — lays the SOURCE-LINEAR thumbnail strip out along the OUTPUT-TIME axis.

One slot per `FreeVideoStudio.Core.Media.OutputTimeline` chunk. Each slot is
a clipping Canvas placed at the chunk's OUTPUT position and width; inside it the strip is
scaled and offset so that exactly the chunk's SOURCE window fills the slot. A half-speed
segment therefore shows its frames spread over twice the width, and a freeze shows the held
frame stretched across the whole hold — which is what the exported file looks like.

A freeze chunk covers a hair of source time by construction, so scaling by its true source
width would blow the image up astronomically. One frame's worth of source time is estimated
from the strip geometry instead (frames are laid out at the strip's own height and a 16:9
aspect), which shows the frozen frame rather than a smear.

Degrades safely: on ANY failure the lane falls back to the plain stretched strip, because a
mis-drawn background must never block editing.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/AppServices.cs

### AppServices — COMPOSITION_01, AOTSAFETY_01, COMPOSITION_02 (line 12)

COMPOSITION_01 — THE ONE PLACE THE OBJECT GRAPH IS BUILT.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
**WHY A HAND-WRITTEN ROOT AND NOT A DI CONTAINER.** An audit found **3 interfaces and 183
static mutable members** across ~90,000 lines, with every collaborator resolved by
`new`-ing it at its use site or by reaching for a static. That is the reason the App layer
has no tests: there is nowhere to substitute anything.

The obvious fix is `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection`. It is rejected here for two
specific reasons, not out of preference:
  1. **Mandate #1 — single binary, NativeAOT, `TrimMode=full`.** A container resolves by
     `Type` at run time. Every resolution is a trim-analyser liability, and the
     project's own `AOTSAFETY_01` block says warnings here are fixed, never muted.
  2. **A container hides the graph.** This one is ~30 lines and can be read in full. When
     the question is "what does MainWindow actually depend on", a file you can read beats a
     registration list you have to execute.
Constructing everything explicitly costs one line per service and buys compile-time proof that
the graph is complete.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

**⚠️ COMPOSITION_02 — `Current` IS A MIGRATION SHIM WITH A DELETION DATE.**
A static accessor is a service locator, and a service locator is the anti-pattern this class
exists to retire. It is here because ~25,000 lines of existing code-behind are constructed by
Avalonia's own lifetime and by XAML, neither of which can pass constructor arguments. Rewriting
all of that in the same change that introduces the root would make the change unreviewable.

The contract for the transition is therefore explicit:
  • NEW code — every view-model, every service — takes its dependencies as CONSTRUCTOR
    PARAMETERS. It must never touch `Current`.
  • LEGACY window code-behind may read `Current` until its view-model is extracted.
  • `Current` is DELETED at the end of the view-model extraction phase. The
    architecture test `NoNewServiceLocatorUsage` holds the line by failing the build if the
    number of call sites ever goes UP.

### AppServices.Current — COMPOSITION_02 (line 55)

⚠️ MIGRATION SHIM — see COMPOSITION_02 on the class. Legacy code-behind only.
New code takes an `AppServices` (or the individual interface) in its constructor.

Builds the production graph. Called exactly once, from `Program.RunUiAsync`, AFTER

The ordering matters: `ApplicationPaths.EnsureWritableDirectories` must

Test seam: installs a graph assembled from fakes. Mirrors `Initialize` but takes

### AvaloniaWindowProvider — INJSEAM_03 (line 184)

INJSEAM_03 — resolves "the window a message belongs to" from Avalonia's desktop lifetime.

Preference order, and the reason for each:
  1. The window that currently has OS focus. A notice about an operation the user just started
     belongs on the window they are looking at.
  2. `MainWindow`. The suite's companion windows can close while their background work is
     still finishing; the main window is the last one standing.
  3. Any open window at all.
  4. `null` — startup, or after the last window closed. Callers MUST tolerate this and fall
     back to the log. Throwing here would make the fault reporter itself a source of faults.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/BinaryPathProbe.cs

### BinaryPathProbe — BINPATH_01 (line 8)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
BINPATH_01 — WHERE THE APP LOOKS FOR ITS BUNDLED ffmpeg/ffprobe, AND THE FACT THAT IT DOES NOT
AGREE WITH ITSELF.

⚠️⚠️ THIS TYPE EXISTS TO MAKE A DIVERGENCE VISIBLE, NOT TO RESOLVE IT. ⚠️⚠️

There are THREE different implementations of "find the bundled binary" in this solution:

  1. `Core/Infrastructure/BinaryPathResolver.Resolve` — searches
     `<baseDir>/<dir>/<file>` then the five-level source-root fallback.
  2. `CropToolWindow.ResolveBinaryPath` — EIGHT candidates, rooted at
     `Environment.ProcessPath`'s directory, probing `preferred`, `backend`,
     `frontend`, the process directory itself, the source root, then two
     `Environment.CurrentDirectory` variants.
  3. `VoiceOverWindow.ResolveBinaryPath` — FOUR candidates, and it roots the PREFERRED
     probe at `AppContext.BaseDirectory` where the Crop Tool roots it at the PROCESS
     directory.

THOSE TWO ROOTS ARE NOT THE SAME DIRECTORY. This app publishes `SelfContained` with
`PublishAot`; for a single-file host, `AppContext.BaseDirectory` can point at the
extraction directory while `Environment.ProcessPath` points at the .exe the user launched.
Two windows of the same application can therefore resolve DIFFERENT ffmpeg binaries, or one can
find it where the other reports failure — and the symptom is an inscrutable FFmpeg error in one
feature only.

⚠️ THE TWO BODIES BELOW ARE MOVED VERBATIM AND KEPT SEPARATE ON PURPOSE. Picking one search
order for both is a BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, not a refactor: whichever window currently depends on the
order it has would start resolving differently, and which one is "right" depends on how the
product is actually installed and launched — something that must be verified on a real install,
not decided from the source. Consolidating them is the follow-up task; this step only ends the
situation where the divergence is invisible because the two copies sit 5,000 lines apart in two
different files.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

A corner overlay is SIMULTANEOUS with the gameplay: this presenter never pauses, seeks or
swaps the one mpv player (that is `MemePreviewDirector`'s job, and only for full-screen
memes). It draws the meme's frames in an `Image` laid over the video host, positioned
with `MemeOverlayLayout` — the same box the export's `overlay` filter uses —

clock, so scrubbing, pausing and playing all stay in step without any timer of its own.

The presenter acquires and holds a lease on what is currently displayed, releasing it immediately
when the window or span changes, or when the presenter is hidden, detached or disposed.

MEMEMODE_01 / CACHEBOUND_05 — corner-preview frames, decoded in bounded time/frame windows off the UI thread:

- Windows are `WindowDurationSeconds` seconds at `Fps` fps.
- Max dimensions are `Width` x `MaxHeight` with aspect ratio preserved, eliminating unbounded pixel growth.
- Offscreen window bytes are budgeted in `Store` (`DefaultMemoryBudgetBytes`), evicting LRU unleased windows.
- Concurrent decodes are throttled by a semaphore to at most `MaxConcurrentDecoders`.
- In-flight decodes for the same key are coalesced so requests never duplicate work.
- FFmpeg subprocesses are bounded by timeout, killed and reaped via child tracking on abort/timeout.

### CropGeometry — CROPGEOM_01 (line 9)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
CROPGEOM_01 — pure geometry for the crop editor: edge snapping, rectangle normalisation and
the aspect-locked diagonal drag delta.

Extracted from `CropToolWindow`. None of them reads window state.

⚠️ SNAP DISTANCES AND THE ASPECT FORMULA ARE CALIBRATED FEEL, NOT ARBITRARY. `SnapAxis`
decides when a dragged edge "grabs"; changing its threshold changes how the tool feels under
the hand, which is a product decision. `DiagonalWidthDelta` resolves a two-axis pointer
delta into the single width change an aspect-locked resize allows — get it wrong and a corner

### CropGeometry.SnapThreshold — CROPGEOM_01 (line 25)

CROPGEOM_01 — how close, in UI pixels, a dragged edge must come before it snaps.
Moved with `SnapAxis`, its only consumer. This is calibrated feel: raising it
makes edges grab from further away and makes fine positioning harder; lowering it makes
snapping feel unreliable. Do not treat it as an arbitrary default.

### CropGeometry.DiagonalWidthDelta — RESIZEFEEL_01 (line 73)

RESIZEFEEL_01 — how far a corner drag has moved ALONG the box's own diagonal.

The old code passed only `dx` and ignored `dy` entirely, so dragging a corner
straight down did nothing at all and dragging it diagonally moved the box by only the
horizontal part of the gesture. That is most of the "unresponsive, unstable" feel: the box
does not follow the pointer, it follows the pointer's shadow on the X axis.

Projecting onto the diagonal is the right answer for a ratio-locked box, because the corner
can only ever travel along that line. The pointer is then free to wander off it — the user
drags roughly outwards and the box grows smoothly outwards — which is exactly how every
other editor behaves.

**dx:** Pointer delta on X since the gesture started.
**dy:** Pointer delta on Y since the gesture started.
**aspect:** height ÷ width of the locked ratio.
**Returns:** The change in WIDTH the drag represents.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/CtsSlot.cs

### CtsSlot — CTSSLOT_01 (line 6)

CTSSLOT_01 — one "current operation" cancellation slot.

The pattern `_cts?.Cancel(); _cts = new CancellationTokenSource();` appeared in several
windows and never disposed the source it replaced (nor the last one on close). A
`CancellationTokenSource` owns a lazily created wait handle, a timer when
`CancelAfter` is used, and every token registration made against it (HttpClient, linked
sources). Left to the finaliser — a poor fit for NativeAOT — they pile up over a long session.

`Renew` cancels AND disposes the previous source and hands out a fresh token.
`Dispose` (call it from the owner's Closed/Dispose) cancels and disposes the last
one. Operations keep only the `CancellationToken` they were given, so a token whose
source was disposed after cancellation still reports `IsCancellationRequested` correctly.
Not thread-safe by design: every owner uses it from the UI thread.

### CtsSlot.Renew (line 30)

Cancels and disposes the previous operation's source and starts a new one.

### CtsSlot.Token (line 39)

The token of the current operation, or `CancellationToken.None` when idle.

### CtsSlot.Cancel (line 42)

Cancels the current operation (if any) and releases its source.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/DebouncedStateWriter.cs

### DebouncedStateWriter — WIZVOLDEBOUNCE_01 (line 13)

WIZVOLDEBOUNCE_01 — WRITE-BEHIND FOR SESSION-STATE PROPERTIES DRIVEN BY A UI CONTROL.

A slider fires `ValueProperty` on every pointer move. Persisting each one synchronously
(`StateTransferStore.UpdatePropertiesSync`) acquired the cross-process state mutex and ran an
atomic write with `Flush(flushToDisk: true)` ON THE UI DISPATCHER, per move. This class owns
the replacement: `Queue` only stores the latest payload and restarts a trailing-edge
timer; when it elapses the payload goes to `UpdatePropertiesAsync` on the thread pool.

⚠️ The pending payload is a FIELD, not a closure capture — a timer built once around a captured
local would persist the FIRST value of the drag forever. Writes are chained so two flushes can
never reorder on disk. When constructed with an owner window, a payload still pending when the
window closes is flushed (dispatched, never awaited).

WIZVOLDEBOUNCE_01 — the trailing-edge window. Matches `MasterVolumePersistence`.

### DebouncedStateWriter.Pending (line 49)

The last background write chain; completes when every dispatched write has settled.

### DebouncedStateWriter.Queue (line 52)

UI thread. Replaces the pending payload and restarts the debounce. Never touches disk.

### DebouncedStateWriter.Flush (line 60)

UI thread. Hands any pending payload to the background chain. Never blocks.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/FilmLanePresenter.cs

### FilmLanePresenter — FILMPIXEL_01, LANECACHE_02, CACHEBOUND_04, LANEINSTANCE_01 (line 14)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
FILMPIXEL_01 (04 UI-MERGERQUEUE, 2026-10-11) — THE MERGER FILMSTRIP LANE, RECONCILED, NOT REBUILT.

`Sync` reconciles the lane with the new tile plan by the clip's width-independent cache key
(LANECACHE_02) instead of clearing it:
  • a tile whose slice and slot count did not change keeps its `Image`s untouched;
  • a moved or resized tile is re-laid from the SAME source (cached strip or the strip still
    streaming) — the cache is not even consulted again, its lease is kept;
  • a tile off the lane is culled; a clip no longer planned has its images removed.
Leases (CACHEBOUND_04): every tile showing a CACHED strip holds exactly one lease; when its images
leave the lane the lease is closed one dispatcher turn later (Background), after the lane dropped its
`CroppedBitmap`s — so an evicted strip is never disposed under an image on screen. A strip still
streaming is shown without a lease and adopted (`Adopt`) when it lands in the cache.
A stream or cache result for a clip not in the current plan never paints. UI thread only.

LANEINSTANCE_01 (2026-10-11) — tiles are OCCURRENCES, strips are SOURCES. Tiles, layout and leases are
keyed by `LaneTile.Occurrence`, so a clip queued twice (same file, same trim → same
`LaneTile.CacheKey`) is drawn twice; before, both were indexed by the cache key and the
second occurrence silently overwrote the first. Everything that comes from the SOURCE — a streamed
frame, a cached or adopted strip — is keyed by the cache key and FANS OUT to every planned occurrence
of it, and each tile showing a cached strip holds ITS OWN lease (an eviction can never dispose a strip
another occurrence still shows). `Sync` hands back at most ONE missing tile per cache key, so
identical occurrences never start a second decode. Reconciliation matches occurrences exactly first,
then lets an unmatched new occurrence ADOPT an unmatched old tile of the SAME source (a reorder that
renumbers clips keeps its images and lease); an old tile is never reused for a different source.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/FilmStripSource.cs

### FilmStripSource — FILMPIXEL_01, LANEINSTANCE_01 (line 11)

FILMPIXEL_01 (04 UI-MERGERQUEUE, 2026-10-11) — ONE streamed ffmpeg strip per clip, shared by every lane run.

A resize or a reorder restarts the film lane's `ProgressiveLaneRunner`, which cancels the
old run. When the old run's item owned the `ThumbnailStripGenerator.StreamAsync` process, that
cancel killed ffmpeg mid-strip and the new run started the same decode from frame 0. Here a clip's
stream is a JOB keyed by its width-independent cache key and NOT tied to any run: a superseded run only
stops waiting; a new run joins the job in flight. The job reports to the window through three
UI-thread callbacks — first frame (`onReady`), every frame (`onFrame`), finished
(`onDone`, exactly once) — so painting and caching happen once per clip, not once per run.
ffmpeg stays bounded at `maxParallel` per lane. Only `Dispose` (window closed) cancels.
LANEINSTANCE_01 — jobs stay keyed by the SOURCE (`LaneTile.CacheKey`), never by the occurrence:
a clip queued twice decodes ONCE, and the presenter fans each frame / finished strip out to every occurrence.

(tile, ct, onReady, onFrame) → true when at least one frame landed. Callbacks run on the UI thread.

### GranularEditorVisuals.IsVideoRectUsable — ZOOM_09 (line 137)

The video's actual letterboxed rect inside the overlay canvas (aspect-fit).

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
⚠️ ZOOM_09 — IS THE VIDEO RECT REAL, OR IS IT THE NOT-LAID-OUT FALLBACK?

`GetVideoDisplayRect` returns `Rect(0,0,max(1,cw),max(1,ch))` when the canvas
has not been through a layout pass yet. That fallback is a SQUARE 1x1, and a square is a
perfectly valid-looking rectangle — so every coordinate conversion downstream keeps working
and quietly produces garbage.

THIS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. It is what a real session logged:
    Zoom Placed on segment #1 ... W=284 H=240 src=854x480 mobile=True
The auto-placed box should have been 160x240 (a 2:3 rectangle). 284x240 is 1.18:1 — not 2:3
at all. The arithmetic reproduces exactly from a 1x1 vid: the box works out as 1/3 x 1/2 of
a unit square, and committing multiplies those by the source size, giving 854/3 = 284 and
480/2 = 240. The zoom was written against a video rectangle that did not exist yet.

ANY code that converts between canvas pixels and source pixels MUST check this first.
The threshold is 4, not 1: a 1- or 2-pixel canvas is layout noise, never a real preview.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/LaneDiskCache.cs

### LaneDiskCache — LANECACHE_02, CACHEBOUND_01 (line 12)

LANECACHE_02 (Video-Merger-Migration.md P11) — the Merger's per-clip filmstrip frames (PNG) and
waveform peaks (float32) on disk, so a clip is decoded ONCE, ever: reopening the Merger, reordering,
resizing and restoring a session all paint from here. Files are named by a hash of the lane cache key
(file path + size + write time + kept window), so an edited source file simply misses. Every call is
best-effort: a cache failure is logged and treated as a miss, never as an error. Call only off the UI
thread.

CACHEBOUND_01 — bounded CONTINUOUSLY, not once per process. The prune used to sit behind a
once-per-process interlocked flag: the first write of a process pruned to 800 files and every
later write in that process grew the folder without limit, with no byte budget at all. Now
`LaneDiskStore` keeps a running tally and, whenever a write takes it over EITHER budget
(`MaxFiles` files, `MaxBytes` bytes), runs one serialized background prune
that deletes least-recently-used files down to 90 % of both.

### LaneDiskCache.MaxFiles — CACHEBOUND_01, LANECACHE_02 (line 30)

CACHEBOUND_01 — entry budget (unchanged from LANECACHE_02).

### LaneDiskCache.MaxBytes — CACHEBOUND_01 (line 32)

CACHEBOUND_01 — byte budget (a 90-frame filmstrip PNG is a few hundred KB).

### LaneDiskStore — CACHEBOUND_01, ATOMICBYTES_01 (line 45)

CACHEBOUND_01 — one lane-cache folder under an entry AND a byte budget.

- **LRU:** recency is the file's last-write time; a hit touches it.
- **Atomic writes:** `AtomicJsonFile.WriteBytes` (ATOMICBYTES_01, SYS-ATOMICWRITE's one
shared implementation): GUID-named temp in the same folder → write-through + flush to disk →
`File.Move(overwrite)`. A reader never sees a half-written file under the final name, and a power
cut cannot leave a zero-filled one. No named mutex: the file is disposable cache.
- **Safe concurrent access:** reads open with Read|Write|Delete sharing, so a concurrent replace or
prune of the same file does not fail the reader or the writer; a file that vanishes mid-read is a miss.
Concurrent writers of one key each publish a complete file; the last rename wins.
- **Serialized background prune:** at most one prune runs; a request during a prune makes it
run once more. The first write of a process always prunes (recount after an earlier session), and
orphaned temp files older than `OrphanTempAge` are swept.

### LaneDiskStore.LowWaterFiles (line 86)

Prune target: 90 % of each budget, so a full cache is not re-pruned on every write.

### LaneDiskStore.WhenIdleAsync (line 90)

Completes when no prune is running or queued (tests, diagnostics).

### LaneDiskStore.RequestPrune (line 161)

Starts the background prune, or asks the running one to go round once more.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/LiveMaskCache.cs

### LiveMaskCache — EDITHOT_01, PROJ_11 (line 10)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
EDITHOT_01 — THE LIVE HUD MASK, READ OFF THE UI THREAD.

PROJ_11 records the live mask in every `ProjectDocument`. It was captured by calling
`MaskOverlayManager.ReadLiveMask` inside `ProjectSession.Capture()`, and Capture
runs on EVERY edit tick (every notch of the speed and quality dials). Each tick therefore:
  • took the machine-wide named mutex `StateTransferStore.MutexName` (15 s timeout),
    which the IPC state server holds across a WriteThrough flush and File.Move retries;
  • read `crops_coordinations.conf` from disk;
  • deep-cloned it and SHA-256 fingerprinted it,
all on the UI thread (North Star #6). A slow disk, an antivirus scan or a sibling process
holding the mutex froze the dial.

The rule now:
  • Hot paths (edit capture, undo/redo, autosave) read `Current`. That is a memory
    read of the last snapshot and never blocks.
  • The snapshot is refreshed on a thread-pool thread: at startup, whenever the crop
    configuration file changes on disk (FileSystemWatcher, which covers the Crop Tool, profile
    switches and external edits), and whenever the active profile name differs from the one
    the snapshot was taken under.
  • A user-initiated Save calls `ReadNow`, which reads synchronously. The saved
    .fvsproj therefore always records the mask that is active at the moment of saving. That
    read is PROJ_11's actual guarantee, and a click is not a gesture.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### LiveMaskCache.Current (line 45)

The last mask snapshot. Never touches the disk or a lock. It schedules a background refresh when
the snapshot is missing or was taken under a different active profile.

### LiveMaskCache.ReadNow (line 63)

Synchronous read for user-initiated saves. Updates the snapshot as a side effect.

### LiveMaskCache.RequestRefresh (line 73)

Queues one background refresh. Coalesces: many requests during one read cost one extra read.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/MemeDimensionCache.cs

### MemeDimensionCache — MEMESCAN_01 (line 10)

MEMESCAN_01 — remembers the probed pixel dimensions of every meme file so the scan does not
launch an ffprobe process for a file it has already measured.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
WHY THIS EXISTS. `MemeCatalog.ScanAsync` spawned ONE ffprobe child process per video meme,
strictly serially, with a 15-second timeout each, and it kept nothing. `MediaProber` does
memoise — but the scan allocated a fresh `MediaProber` inside the loop body and dropped it
on the next iteration, so that memoisation was dead code on this path. Every repopulate paid the
full cost again from zero.

The scan is re-entered on window `Loaded` (the cold-start critical path), on every
`MemeDirectory.Changed`, and immediately after a cloud sync — i.e. at the exact moment the
library has just grown to its largest. At roughly 100 ms per CreateProcess+probe on Windows, a
few hundred memes is a multi-second stall on app start, every start, forever.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

**Invalidation is by (length, last-write-time), never by path alone.** A file that was
replaced in place — which is exactly what the cloud delta-sync does when it repairs a truncated
download — must be re-probed or the export would be handed stale geometry.

**⚠️ A cached non-positive dimension is treated as a MISS, never as a hit.**
`MemeCatalog` excludes any video whose probe returned `Width <= 0` with the log line
"would crash export". If this cache could satisfy that guard from a stored zero, a file that
failed to probe once would be permanently, silently excluded — or worse, admitted with zero
geometry. Nothing useful is ever cached for a failed probe.

Written through `AtomicJsonFile.WriteObject` into the consolidated ProgramData root
(`uistate\`), per `docs/05_SYSTEM_LIFECYCLE_STORAGE.md#SYS-ATOMICWRITE` — never
`File.WriteAllText`, which is what leaves a correctly named but zero-filled file after a
power cut. It is inside the same root the installer's "preserve my settings" switch and the
uninstaller's zero-footprint sweep already know about, so neither needs a new special case.

Every method is total: a corrupt, locked or missing cache degrades to "no hits" and the

MEME_02 — remembers, per meme file, whether the user wants it at the Start or the End.

⚠️ WHY A REMEMBERED CHOICE RATHER THAN A NAMING RULE. The alternative was encoding it in the
filename (`… [start].mp4`), which is ugly in the user's folder, breaks the instant anyone
renames a file, and forces the app to rewrite files it does not own. This keeps the decision
in the app's own settings and leaves the user's media untouched.

THE PRECEDENCE IS DELIBERATE:
  1. the user's own choice for this exact file, if they have ever made one — always wins;
  2. otherwise the shipped default (MemeAssets.DefaultsToStart), which knows the bundled memes;
  3. otherwise End, the safe conventional case, which is what every new/unknown meme gets.
Nothing can work out "this is an intro meme" from the video itself — it is a judgement about
meaning — so the only honest options are "the user said so" or "we shipped an opinion".

ATOMICSTATE_01 — the gate around `_cache`.

Every caller today is on the UI thread (`MainWindow.Export.cs`,

said so, and the hazard is not a benign one: `_cache` is a plain
`Dictionary{TKey,TValue}` that `Set` mutates in place while
`Get` may be reading it, and the lazy publish at the end of
`LoadUnlocked` was a non-atomic check-build-publish that two callers could run
concurrently. A single background caller — a future export payload built off the UI
thread, say — turns that into dictionary corruption or an InvalidOperationException raised
from inside a failure path.

⚠️ DISK I/O IS DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THIS LOCK. `Get` is on the export
payload path; a slow or contended disk in `Set` must never serialise it. The
pattern is the one `MemeDimensionCache` already uses: build the snapshot under the
lock, commit it outside.

ATOMICSTATE_01 — the caller MUST hold `_sync`. Returns the live cache

Remembers the user's choice for this file. Their choice wins from now on.

ATOMICSTATE_01 — the commit was `File.WriteAllText`, which opens the target with

loss inside that window did not cost the one entry being changed — it cost EVERY
remembered placement the user had ever set, leaving a correctly named but truncated or
zero-length file behind. `AtomicJsonFile.WriteText` is the protocol

state writer in this solution already uses: unique GUID temp file in the TARGET directory

and it is kept deliberately: the user's click is honoured for this session, and the next
successful Set rewrites the whole map and heals the divergence.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/MemePreviewDirector.cs

### MemePreviewDirector — MEME_07 (line 13)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
MEME_07 — THE MEME CUTAWAY, SHOWN IN THE PREVIEW EXACTLY AS IT WILL BE EXPORTED.

**The problem this solves.** A meme occupies ZERO source seconds and its whole length in
OUTPUT seconds, so `OutputTimeline.OutputToSourceRelative` answers every instant
inside the block with the anchor frame. That is mathematically right and visually useless: the
preview parked on one still while the finished video plays a whole meme, and the user could not
see what they had built until they exported it.

**The approach (option B — one host, swap the file).** Every preview in this app is a single
`MpvVideoView` that owns a libmpv render context, a D3D11 device, WGL/DXGI interop and a
16-texture shared swap chain. A SECOND one, layered over the first, would give a seamless
cutaway and would also double that stack in every window and add a disposal-ordering hazard to
four of them. So instead the ONE host is re-pointed: park the gameplay on the anchor frame,
load the meme, play it through, load the gameplay back at the same anchor frame, carry on.

**The cost, and why it is announced rather than hidden.** Two `loadfile` round-trips per
meme, a few hundred milliseconds each, during which the picture is black. Hiding that would read
as a stutter or a crash. So each swap raises a blocking, unmissable overlay that says what is
happening and clears itself the moment the picture is live again. The user asked for exactly
this: stall visibly, then be flawless.

**⚠️ THE RULE EVERY HOST WINDOW MUST FOLLOW.** While this director is active, mpv is showing
the MEME, so `CurrentTime`, `Duration` and `IsEof` describe the meme file and NOT
the gameplay. Every consumer of those — cut-skip, trim-end-stop, music sync, voice-take sync,
the zoom crop updater, the end-of-video handler — would misfire. So the host's playback tick
must begin with:

```csharp

    if (_memePreview != null && _memePreview.IsActive) { /* hold the caret */ return; }

```

That single early return is what makes this safe, and it is why the caret hold is the only
thing a host is allowed to do while a meme is on screen.

**What deliberately does NOT trigger a cutaway.** Only forward PLAYBACK crossing an anchor
does. Scrubbing, dragging the caret, and every programmatic seek are excluded — detected as a
jump larger than `SeekJumpSec` or a backwards move — because a cutaway that fired
while the user dragged the playhead would make the timeline impossible to scrub, which is the
opposite of the point.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/MemeThumbnailCache.cs

### MemeThumbnailCache — MEMEPICK_01, LIBAVFRAME_04, CACHEBOUND_02 (line 15)

MEMEPICK_01 — small preview pictures for the meme picker, so a meme is chosen by what it looks
like and not by its file name.

- Pictures are decoded straight to `ThumbWidth` pixels wide (never the full
8-megapixel bitmap).
- Videos get ONE frame. LIBAVFRAME_04: decoded in-process by native libav
(`VideoFrameGrabber`: the frame ffmpeg `-ss T -frames:v 1 -vf scale=160:-2` would
output, scaled straight to 160 px by swscale, BGRA → Bitmap), with the ORIGINAL ffmpeg
subprocess (PNG piped on stdout, owned by `ChildProcessTracker`, below normal
priority, killed after `FrameTimeout`) kept as the one-shot fallback. Nothing is
written to disk on either path. `FVS_FRAME_DECODE=ffmpeg|native` forces one path.
- At most `MaxConcurrent` decodes run at once so a large library cannot flood
the machine with ffmpeg processes while the user is editing. A caller that cancels while
waiting for a lane leaves the queue at once (stale picker rows never decode).
- CACHEBOUND_02 — results live in ONE byte-budgeted LRU (`Store`:
`MemoryBudgetBytes` of pixels, at most `MaxEntries` entries), keyed by
path + size + last-write time, so reopening the picker is instant and a replaced file is never
shown with a stale picture (its old entry is retired the moment the new key is stored). The
cache OWNS every bitmap: callers get an `OwnedLruCache{T}.Lease`, and an evicted
bitmap is disposed only after the last lease on it closes, so a picture still bound to an
`Image` is never disposed under it. It used to be a static dictionary that kept every
bitmap of every meme ever shown for the life of the process.

A failure yields null and the picker shows the type icon instead (the failure is cached as a
small negative entry, keyed by mtime, so a replaced file is retried). It never throws, except
the caller's own cancellation.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/OutputFolderResolver.cs

### OutputFolderResolver — ISSUE_04 (line 11)

ISSUE_04 — resolves WHERE a finished video is written, for each sub-application separately.

Resolution order (do not reorder):
  1. The folder saved in settings for THIS app, if it still exists and is writable.
  2. The user's REAL Downloads folder via `KnownFolders.GetDownloads` — this is
     shell-resolved, so a moved Downloads folder, a OneDrive-redirected one, or a Group
     Policy redirected one all resolve correctly. (The old code hardcoded
     %USERPROFILE%\Downloads and was simply wrong on those machines.)
  3. Only if neither is usable: ask the user to pick a folder ("Save As"). Whatever they
     pick is SAVED as the new default for that app, so they are asked exactly once.

Hard rule: this never throws and never crashes the app when Downloads is missing. If the
user cancels the picker it returns null and the caller aborts the export cleanly with the
standard error dialog — it must not fall through into the pipeline with a null path.

Full interactive resolution. Call this once, before starting a render.
Returns the directory to write into, or null if the user cancelled the picker.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/OwnedLruCache.cs

### OwnedLruCache — CACHEBOUND_02 (line 8)

CACHEBOUND_02 (04 UI-MEMESELECT) — a byte-budgeted LRU that OWNS what it stores.

- Every stored value has exactly one owner: this cache. A caller never receives a raw value,
only a `Lease`; the value stays alive while ANY lease on it is open.
- Eviction (budget, replacement of the same identity, `Remove`, `Clear`)
drops the entry from the index at once, but the value is disposed only when its last lease closes.
So a bitmap still bound to a UI control is never disposed under it.
- Leased (pinned) entries are never chosen for budget eviction; the budget therefore bounds
everything NOT currently on screen, and what is on screen is bounded by the viewport.
- One live entry per identity (e.g. a file path): storing a new key for the same identity
(the file was replaced, so size/mtime changed) retires the old one.
- A null value is a cached "no picture" answer (negative entry) with a small fixed cost.

Thread-safe. Values are disposed outside the lock, on the thread that dropped the last reference.

### OwnedLruCache.Lease (line 45)

An open reference to a cached value. Dispose exactly when the value is no longer shown.

### OwnedLruCache.PinnedCount (line 90)

Indexed entries with at least one open lease.

### OwnedLruCache.RetiredAliveCount (line 104)

Entries already evicted from the index whose value waits for its last lease (diagnostics/tests).

### OwnedLruCache.AddAndAcquire (line 121)

Stores `value` (ownership passes to the cache, null = negative answer) and returns a
lease on what is now cached under `key` (null for a negative answer). If a racing
producer stored the same key first, the first value wins and `value` is disposed.

### OwnedLruCache.Remove (line 154)

Retires whatever is cached for `identity` (e.g. the file disappeared).

### OwnedLruCache.RemoveByIdentityPrefix (line 165)

Retires all entries whose identity starts with `prefix` (e.g. all windows of a file).

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/PreviewAudioSync.cs

### PreviewAudioSync — MUSICSYNC_02 (line 7)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
MUSICSYNC_02 — ONE SLAVE-TO-THE-VIDEO RULE FOR EVERY PREVIEW AUDIO PLAYER.

The video (mpv time-pos, mapped to OUTPUT seconds through OutputTimeline) is the master clock.
Every other preview sound (voice-over takes on NAudio, the music bed on its own audio-only mpv)
follows it. Before this they each ran open-loop:
  • voice-over takes on a default WaveOutEvent: 300 ms of buffering, compared against the
    READER position (which runs ahead of what is audible by that buffering), and a 0.5 s
    tolerance. A take could sit up to half a second off the picture before anything corrected it;
  • the music bed never corrected at all during continuous playback.

The rule:
  • Correct by SEEKING only. Never change a follower's playback RATE. Music and voice always
    play at 1.0x. Only the video changes speed.
  • Tolerance `DriftToleranceSec` (≈ 3 frames at 24 fps). A correction needs
    `DriftStrikes` consecutive readings over tolerance, so tick jitter never
    causes a seek.
  • NAudio's reader runs `VoiceReaderLeadSec` ahead of the speaker. That lead is
    subtracted before comparing, and added back when repositioning.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/ProtectedFolderGate.cs

### ProtectedFolderGate — CFASAFE_01 (line 12)

CFASAFE_01 — decides whether the app may write into a folder that Windows Security's
"Controlled folder access" protects (Videos, Music, Documents, Pictures, Desktop), and remembers
a refusal so the app does not knock on that door at every start.

Each refused write makes Windows show the user a "blocked" notification. The app used to try the
same writes at every launch (starter memes into Videos, starter songs into Music, the personal
Desktop icon), so a protected PC showed that notification on every start. Now:

- protection off, or the folder is not a protected one → yes, nothing is tried or stored;
- otherwise ONE real write is tried. Allowed → yes. Refused → no, and the refusal is written
to `controlled_folder_denied.txt` in the preferences folder;
- while that record is younger than `RecheckAfter` and names this program, the
answer stays no WITHOUT another attempt (no notification). It is forgotten when the user opens
Windows Security from the app's notice, so the next start checks again.

Callers then use a folder of the app's own instead (`MemeDirectory`) or Downloads
(`OutputFolderResolver`). The app never changes a Windows Security setting.

Spec: docs/05_SYSTEM_LIFECYCLE_STORAGE.md #SYS-CFASAFE.

### ProtectedFolderGate.RecheckAfter (line 36)

How long a remembered refusal is believed before one new attempt is made.

### ProtectedFolderGate.CanWrite (line 46)

True when the app may write into `folder`. One answer per folder and process.

### ProtectedFolderGate.CanWriteNow (line 54)

The same question for installer code that runs as another program (the update worker): one
real attempt when the folder is protected, nothing remembered, no notice.

### ProtectedFolderGate.DenialIsFresh (line 82)

Pure (unit-tested): a marker is believed when it names this program and is younger than
`RecheckAfter` (and not from the future). Line 1 = UTC time, line 2 = program path.

### ProtectedFolderGate.ForgetDenial (line 98)

Forgets a remembered refusal: the next start makes one fresh attempt.

### ProtectedFolderGate.FfmpegCanWrite — CFAFFMPEG_01 (line 140)

CFAFFMPEG_01 — the exported video is written by FFmpeg, a SECOND program, and Windows' allowed
list is per program. A user who allowed only Free Video Studio got an export that failed at the
very end. Before a render into a protected folder, FFmpeg itself writes (and the app deletes) a
tiny silent probe file there, once per folder and run; refused → the caller uses Downloads and
shows the notice that names both programs. Nothing is tried when protection is off or the folder
is not protected.

### ProtectedFolderGate.TakePendingNotice (line 193)

True once per process after a NEW refusal was found: the caller shows the notice.

### ProtectedFolderGate.ShowNoticeAsync (line 196)

Explains the refusal once and offers to open Windows Security on its "Ransomware protection"

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/SecretProtector.cs

### SecretProtector — KEYPROTECT_01 (line 7)

KEYPROTECT_01 (docs/05 SYS-AISETTINGS) — keeps the Gemini API key out of settings.json as plain text.

On Windows the key is sealed with DPAPI (`CryptProtectData`, CURRENT USER scope, an
app-specific entropy) and stored as `"dpapi1:" + base64`. Only the same Windows account on the
same machine can open it, so a copied settings file, a quarantined corrupt copy or a support
bundle no longer carries a usable key. Direct P/Invoke to crypt32 — no extra package, NativeAOT-safe.

Text without the prefix is legacy plain text (schema ≤ 13) and is returned as-is; the settings
migration re-seals it. Off Windows (test hosts only — the product is Windows-only) the value is stored
with the `"plain1:"` prefix so it is still recognisable and never mistaken for a sealed blob.

Never throws, never logs the secret. An undecryptable blob (another user / machine) reads as
empty: the user is asked for the key again rather than shown an error with the blob in it.

### SecretProtector.IsProtectedForm (line 29)

True when `stored` is already in a protected (prefixed) form.

be ordinary mutable objects shared by every window: "mutate only through Update" was a comment plus
a regex test that cannot see aliases kept across methods or nested objects (KeyBinds, Defaults, AI
configs). Every settings object now derives from this base. A draft — what `SettingsManager.Update`
hands its patch, a JSON clone, a view-model's pending copy — is writable as before. The snapshot is
`Freeze`-ed (recursively) before it is published, after which ANY property write throws
and names the property, so a stray write is a loud defect instead of a silent divergence between
what the screen shows, what is saved and what the app uses.

WHY THIS EXISTS: the boot scan used to be the ONLY input to encoder selection, and when it
crashed (see ChildProcessTracker G01) it reported "CPU" — permanently, silently, with no
way for the user to say "no, I have an RTX, use it". Every export on an affected machine
ran on libx264 while the UI gave no indication anything was wrong.

"Auto" must remain the default. A non-Auto value wins over the scan result unconditionally
and is passed straight through to `ProcessWorker.HardwareStrategy` /
`MergerWorker.HardwareStrategy`. If the chosen encoder is genuinely absent from the
bundled FFmpeg, `EncoderManager.EncoderPreflightError` blocks the export with a clear
message instead of silently doing something else.

and the scan, the starter delivery and a recovery restore await `WhenReadyAsync`,
so they see either the old layout or the finished move — never a half-moved folder. It no
longer hides inside the folder lookup.
- A Settings override that points AT the old default is cleared, so the user follows the
move. Any other custom folder is the user's and is left alone.
- Never overwrites: a same-named file already in the new folder wins. An identical copy
in the old folder is removed; a DIFFERENT one is left where it is and logged.
- The old folders are removed only when empty.
- The move is recorded in migration-paths.json (UPGRADE_05), so saved projects and
recovery files that name a meme by its old full path still open it.

A failure is logged and never blocks the app; the next launch retries.

(SpeedPresetButtons.NativeDefaultSpeed), so a strict bound is what keeps the default OUT of
"Normal" and in "Slight Boost". Do not tidy that into a uniform comparison.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/ThemeResources.cs

### ThemeResources — THEME_01 (line 10)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THEME_01 — THE ONE SAFE WAY TO PULL A BRUSH OR COLOUR OUT OF THE THEME FROM CODE-BEHIND.

⚠️ WHY THIS EXISTS — READ BEFORE WRITING `FindResource` ANYWHERE.
`FindResource` DOES NOT RETURN NULL WHEN A KEY IS MISSING. It returns
`AvaloniaProperty.UnsetValue`, an instance of `Avalonia.UnsetValueType`. So this,
which reads like defensive code, is a live grenade:

    Foreground = (IBrush?)Application.Current?.FindResource("AppTextMutedBrush") ?? Brushes.Gray;

The `?? Brushes.Gray` never runs. The CAST fires first and throws:
    InvalidCastException: Unable to cast object of type 'Avalonia.UnsetValueType'
                          to type 'Avalonia.Media.IBrush'
That exact line stopped the Video Merger from opening at all.

AND THE KEY MOST LIKELY TO GO MISSING IS A PERFECTLY GOOD ONE. Half of this app's brushes live
inside `ResourceDictionary.ThemeDictionaries` in AvaloniaApp.axaml — AppSurfaceBrush,
AppPanelBrush, AppBorderBrush, AppTextPrimaryBrush, AppTextMutedBrush, AppControlTrackBrush and
friends. A theme-scoped resource can only be resolved against a THEME VARIANT. Ask without one,
or ask before the app's variant has settled during startup, and you get UnsetValue back for a
key that is sitting right there in the file.

THE RULES THIS CLASS ENFORCES:
  (T1) Use `TryFindResource`, never `FindResource`. It reports failure instead of handing back
       a sentinel that looks like a value and explodes at the cast.
  (T2) Always pass a ThemeVariant, and prefer the CONTROL's over the Application's. A control
       already attached to a window knows its own variant even while the app's is still
       settling, and it also picks up any ThemeVariantScope it happens to sit inside.
  (T3) Always take a fallback. A missing brush must degrade to a readable colour — never to a
       crash, and never to an invisible control.

USAGE — pass the control that will DISPLAY the brush as the host:
    status.Foreground = ThemeResources.Brush(status, "AppTextMutedBrush", Brushes.Gray);
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### ThemeResources.Brush (line 48)

Resolves a brush against `host`'s current theme variant, falling back to
`fallback` if the key is missing, is not a brush, or the lookup throws.
Never throws. Never returns null.

### ThemeResources.Colour (line 77)

Same contract as `Brush`, for raw Color tokens. Accepts either a Color resource
or a SolidColorBrush resource, so a token can be redefined as either without breaking here.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/ViewportThumbnailLoader.cs

### ViewportThumbnailLoader — CACHEBOUND_03 (line 10)

CACHEBOUND_03 (04 UI-MEMESELECT) — loads thumbnails for the rows a virtualizing list has actually
realized, plus `Prefetch` rows either side, and lets go of the rest.

The meme picker used to walk EVERY scanned meme and decode its picture whether or not it was ever
scrolled into view, and kept every result. With a few thousand memes that is thousands of decodes
(and, for videos, libav/ffmpeg runs) for a dialog the user may close after one click.

- **Feed:** the list's container events — `Realized` (prepared at an index),
`IndexChanged`, `Cleared` — and `SetRows` whenever the shown list
changes (filter, re-scan). Each change schedules ONE coalesced reconcile on the UI thread.
- **Wanted** = realized rows first (top to bottom), then near-visible rows by distance.
A wanted row with no request starts one (the decode limit itself lives in the cache's lanes).
- **Released** = any row further than `KeepMargin` rows from the realized range, or
no longer in the list: its pending request is CANCELLED (it leaves the decode queue) and a shown
picture is unbound from the row first and its lease closed one dispatcher turn later (idle
priority), so the `Image` has dropped it before the cache may dispose it.
- A result that arrives for a row that was released, superseded or disposed meanwhile is
handed straight back (its lease closed) and never assigned.

Single-threaded: every public member and every completion runs on the thread behind
`post` (the UI thread in the app, a pumped queue in tests).

### ViewportThumbnailLoader.Prefetch (line 76)

### ViewportThumbnailLoader.KeepMargin (line 78)

Rows beyond this distance from the realized range give their picture back (hysteresis ≥ Prefetch).

### ViewportThumbnailLoader.ActiveCount (line 81)

Rows with a request in flight or a picture held (tests/diagnostics).

### ViewportThumbnailLoader.SetRows (line 87)

The list now shows `rows` (call BEFORE handing them to the list).

### ViewportThumbnailLoader.Reconcile (line 124)

Starts what is wanted, releases what is far away. Normally called through the coalesced post.

### ViewportThumbnailLoader.Dispose (line 191)

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/VoiceOverAudioTools.cs

### VoiceOverAudioTools — VOTOOLS_01 (line 7)

VOTOOLS_01 — peak decoding, take-file cleanup, preview-player retirement and the remembered
voice-protection choices, lifted out of `VoiceOverWindow`.

That window is 3,792 lines and 116 fields, and what makes it risky is not its size but that it
owns LIVE MICROPHONE AND PLAYBACK HANDLES alongside UI state. These members touch none of that
— they are file and buffer work — so moving them shrinks the surface that has to be reasoned
about together with device lifetime.

⚠️ `TryDeleteFile`, `RetirePreviewPlayersAsync` AND `RetireGenerationCts` ARE
TOTAL BY CONTRACT. They run on teardown paths; an exception escaping any of them turns "a take
could not be cleaned up" into a failed close. Bodies moved verbatim — do not add rethrows.

⚠️ Take WAV files live in TWO directories with different retention rules (the temp root and the
voice-over directory). Deleting from the wrong one destroys a recording the user still needs.

### VoiceOverAudioTools.DecodePeaks — VOTAKE_01 (line 25)

VOTAKE_01 — reduces a WAV to `buckets` absolute peaks (0..1).
Runs on a worker thread; touches no interface state.

### VoiceOverAudioTools.TryDeleteFile — ISSUE_05 (line 58)

ISSUE_05 — deletes a temp take, tolerating a briefly-still-held file handle.

The recorder now closes its WAV writer in an ordered shutdown, but Windows can hold a
handle open for a few more milliseconds after the last Dispose. A single attempt therefore
used to lose the race now and then and leave abandoned takes accumulating in the temp
folder forever, because every failure was swallowed by a bare `catch`.

### VoiceOverAudioTools.RetireGenerationCts — LEAK_02, CANCEL_01 (line 99)

LEAK_02 — cancel a superseded generation, then dispose it OFF the interface thread.

⚠️ NEVER call `CancellationTokenSource.Dispose()` directly from an event handler here.
Dispose BLOCKS until every callback raised by Cancel() has finished, and those callbacks
marshal back to the interface thread — so the interface thread ends up waiting for itself.
That is the exact deadlock that froze the Granular Speed Editor earlier (see CANCEL_01);
it is a real, reproduced bug in this codebase, not a theoretical one.

Handing the disposal to a worker thread keeps the tidy-up without the wait: nothing on that
thread is holding the interface hostage, so Cancel's callbacks are free to complete.

### VoiceOverAudioTools.FormatClock — VOTL_01 (line 124)

VOTL_01 — formats a clock the same way the main screen's timeline does, so the two windows
read as one product. Always hh:mm:ss; a leading sign is the caller's business.

VOPROT_02 — stores the applied choices as the "last time" values, but ONLY for a checkbox

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/WaveformLanePresenter.cs

### WaveformLanePresenter — WAVEPIXEL_01, LANECACHE_02, LANEINSTANCE_01 (line 15)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
WAVEPIXEL_01 (04 UI-MERGERQUEUE, 2026-10-11) — THE MERGER WAVEFORM LANE, RECONCILED, NOT REBUILT.

The lane used to be cleared and rebuilt on every layout change, each tile a `Path` of
2 × peaks points made on the UI thread. Now `Sync` RECONCILES the lane against the new
tile plan, keyed by the clip's width-independent cache key (LANECACHE_02):
  • a tile still in the plan keeps its Path — a move or resize only sets Left/Width (Stretch.Fill);
  • its levels are re-reduced only when its pixel columns drift past
    `WaveformEnvelope.RebuildRatio`, and the reduction runs on the thread pool;
  • a tile off the lane (x ≥ lane width or x1 ≤ 0) is culled; a tile narrower than
    `DenseTilePx` gets NO Path of its own — all such slivers share ONE lane-wide path;
  • every completion is guarded: a reduction for an older request, a cleared lane (epoch) or a
    clip no longer in the plan is dropped, never painted.
Total geometry is O(visible device pixels): ≤ `WaveformEnvelope.PointCount` per tile.
UI thread only (except the pure reductions it schedules).

LANEINSTANCE_01 (2026-10-11) — tiles are keyed by the clip OCCURRENCE (`LaneTile.Occurrence`),
peaks by the SOURCE (`LaneTile.CacheKey`). A clip queued twice with the same trim used to
collapse into one tile because both occurrences shared the cache key. Now each occurrence owns its own
Path (and its own pixel-column reduction), a delivered peak list fans out to EVERY planned occurrence of
that source, `Sync` asks for at most one fetch per source, and an unmatched new occurrence may
adopt an unmatched old tile of the SAME source only (renumbering reorder = no new work).
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### WaveformLanePresenter.DenseTilePx (line 42)

Tiles narrower than this share the lane's one dense path instead of owning a Path.

### WaveformLanePresenter.PointCount (line 75)

### WaveformLanePresenter.ReductionsScheduled (line 87)

Reductions scheduled since construction.

### WaveformLanePresenter.Sync (line 100)

Reconciles the lane with `plan`. `cachedPeaks` returns a clip's
cached peaks or null; the tiles it cannot serve are returned — the caller fetches them and hands
them back through `Deliver`.

### WaveformLanePresenter.Deliver — LANEINSTANCE_01 (line 170)

A worker finished a SOURCE's peaks (and reduced them off the dispatcher to `columns`).
LANEINSTANCE_01 — fanned out to every planned occurrence of that source; the pre-reduced levels are
reused where an occurrence needs the same column count, the others reduce their own. Dropped when no
occurrence of the source is in the plan — a stale completion never paints.

### WaveformLanePresenter.Clear (line 197)

Empties the lane; every reduction still in flight is dropped (epoch).

Puts a known tile where its plan says and makes sure its levels match its pixel width.

The O(peaks) work runs on the thread pool; only the O(columns) result comes back.

### WaveformLanePresenter.BuildPath (line 272)

### WaveformLanePresenter.ScheduleDense (line 317)

Many slivers finishing in one burst rebuild the shared path once, not once each.

### WaveformLanePresenter.RebuildDense (line 330)

Every sliver tile in ONE path, in lane pixels (no stretch). Each is scaled to its own loudest
column so it reads like a Stretch.Fill tile. O(sum of sliver columns) ≤ O(lane device pixels).

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/WaveformPeakSource.cs

### WaveformPeakSource — WAVEPIXEL_01 (line 11)

WAVEPIXEL_01 (04 UI-MERGERQUEUE) — ONE peak fetch per clip, shared by every lane run.

A resize or a reorder restarts the waveform lane's `ProgressiveLaneRunner`, which cancels
the old run. When the old run's item owned the ffmpeg process, that cancel killed it and the new run
started the same extraction again. Here a clip's fetch (disk cache → ffmpeg → disk write) is keyed by
its width-independent cache key and NOT tied to any run: a superseded run only stops WAITING; a new
run for the same clip joins the fetch already in flight. ffmpeg stays bounded at
`maxParallel` per lane. Only `Dispose` (window closed) cancels a fetch.
The disk write completes before the fetch does, so a later miss in the memory cache finds the file.

LANEINSTANCE_01 — keyed by the SOURCE (cache key): every occurrence of the same clip shares one fetch.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Infrastructure/WindowsAudioSessionSync.cs

### WindowsAudioSessionSync — VOLSYNC_01, VOLCURVE_01 (line 10)

VOLSYNC_01 — the app's master volume and its entry in the Windows Volume Mixer are ONE control.

Before: the app attenuated inside mpv and never touched its Windows audio session, so the
two volumes simply multiplied and neither ever moved when the other did.

Now this process's audio session (every player, the voice-over takes and the UI sounds share
it — one process, one default session) carries the master:

- app slider → session level = (position/100)³ (VOLCURVE_01's perceptual gain; the session
  volume is LINEAR amplitude per Microsoft's "Audio-Tapered Volume Controls"), shared mute →
  session mute;
- Volume Mixer → app slider = ∛level × 100, Mixer mute → shared mute. Polled every
  `PollMs` ms on one dedicated MTA thread that owns every COM call;
- while it works, `MpvIpcClient.MasterAppliedBySystem` is true and players carry
  only their balances, so the master is never applied twice. If Core Audio is unavailable (no
  device, not Windows, any COM failure) the flag goes false and players apply the master
  themselves — the old behaviour, with the new curve.

Raw vtable calls (the TaskbarProgress pattern): NativeAOT-safe, no ComWrappers.

### MainWindow._timelineRedrawQueued — TIMELINEDRAW_01 (line 290)

TIMELINEDRAW_01 — one rebuild per frame, not one per call.

WHAT WAS WRONG. `UpdateTimelineMarkers` posts a FULL teardown and rebuild
of the timeline visual tree — every trim marker, cut glyph, meme block, music block, scale
tick and label, plus the ~32 pointer handlers attached to them — and it is invoked from
THIRTY call sites across five partial files. Nothing coalesced those posts, so a single user
action that touched two pieces of state (release a marker -> update markers -> save recovery
-> update dragging visuals) queued two, three or four complete rebuilds into the same frame.
Worse, the 100 ms playback timer re-checks `canvas.Children.Count == 0`
(MainWindow.axaml.cs) to decide whether to draw — and because the rebuild is DEFERRED, that
count is still zero when it looks, so it posted again on the next tick, and the next.

This flag collapses any number of requests in one dispatcher turn into exactly one
rebuild. It is read and written only on the UI thread: all thirty call sites are event
handlers, key handlers or UI methods, and the reset happens inside the posted callback,
which is by definition on the UI thread. No interlocked access is needed or wanted.

⚠️ THE GUARDS MOVED WITH INTENT. `RenderTimelineMarkersCore` re-reads the
canvas, the IpcClient and the duration when it actually runs, instead of capturing them at
request time. Before, `duration` was captured OUTSIDE the post and used inside it, so a
rebuild could draw against a duration that was already stale by the time it ran. Coalescing
widens that window, so the read had to move; re-reading is strictly more correct either
way.

### MainWindow.TimelineRedrawGestureWaitCeilingMs — TIMELINEDRAW_01, ISSUE_13 (line 317)

TIMELINEDRAW_01 — ceiling on how long a queued rebuild will wait for a gesture to finish.

The deferral below re-queues while `IsMarkerGestureActive` is true. If a drag
flag ever LEAKS — pointer capture lost without the handler clearing it, which this codebase
has a documented history of (ISSUE_13) — an unbounded wait would mean the timeline silently
never redraws again for the rest of the session. That is a worse failure than the one the
deferral prevents, so after this long the rebuild happens anyway: the outcome degrades to
exactly the pre-TIMELINEDRAW_01 behaviour instead of to a dead timeline.

### MainWindow._timelineRedrawDeadlineTicks (line 329)

Tick count at which the currently queued rebuild stops deferring and just runs.

### MainWindow.QueueTimelineRedrawPass — TIMELINEDRAW_01, THUMB_02 (line 346)

TIMELINEDRAW_01 — posts the one pending rebuild, deferring past any live marker gesture.

THUMB_02 is the reason this exists at the RENDER end rather than at the call sites.
Suppressing a mid-gesture rebuild used to be the caller's job, and only ONE of the thirty
call sites did it; every other path could destroy the control holding pointer capture and
kill the drag under the user's cursor. Checking here covers all thirty at once.

⚠️ DEFER, DO NOT DROP. A dropped request would leave the timeline showing stale state
whenever the last request of a gesture happened to arrive before the flags cleared. Keeping
`_timelineRedrawQueued` true and re-posting at Background priority means the
rebuild lands on the first idle turn after the gesture ends, costs one boolean read per idle
turn while it waits, and can never queue a second rebuild alongside itself.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/MainWindow.Controls.cs

### MainWindow — MVVM_03, MVVM_02, QUALITY_04, MVVM_01 (line 11)

MVVM_03 — the cached control accessors for `MainWindow`.

⚠️ IN ITS OWN FILE ON PURPOSE. MVVM_02 caps window code-behind and the cap may only ever
fall, so adding these to the code-behind — even while REMOVING lookups from it — would
have pushed several files past their ceiling and forced the ratchet up. A ratchet that
gets raised to accommodate an improvement stops being a ratchet.

These replace repeated `this.FindControl<T>("Name")` calls — some controls were
resolved by string fifteen times in one file. Each lookup walks the visual tree and can
return null, so a renamed control compiled cleanly and produced a dead button at run time
(QUALITY_04). Now a rename breaks in exactly one place.

This is a STEP toward MVVM_01, not the destination. The end state is a binding to a
view-model property; until then, one resolution per control means the eventual binding
replaces one accessor instead of hunting every call site.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/MainWindow.Export.cs

### MainWindow.ProcessVideoAsync — EXPORTSESSION_01, EXPORTSESSION_02, CANCELREG_01 (line 26)

EXPORTSESSION_01 — THE SINGLE-FLIGHT GATE AND THE CANCELLATION-TOKEN-SOURCE OWNER is now
`FreeVideoStudio.App.Services.ExportCoordinator` (EXPORTSESSION_02).

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Everything about an export's LIFETIME lives in the coordinator; everything about its CONTENT
lives in `ProcessVideoCoreAsync`. The three defects this split closed were all
lifetime defects: a second pipeline started while the first was still being cancelled; the
second export disposed the CancellationTokenSource the first worker was still registered on
(the CANCELREG_01 hang); nothing waited for the pipeline before window teardown.

THE RULE, unchanged: the token source is disposed only after the pipeline Task has completed,
by the coordinator and by nothing else. This method restores the UI in exactly one place —
after StartAsync returns, i.e. after the coordinator reports Idle — so "the overlay is gone"
can never again mean anything except "the pipeline has stopped".
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/MainWindow.PreviewAudio.cs

### MainWindow — MUSICSYNC_01, MUSICSYNC_02, CUTS_02 (line 8)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
MUSICSYNC_01 / MUSICSYNC_02 — PREVIEW AUDIO FOLLOWS THE VIDEO, IN OUTPUT TIME.

The master clock is the video player's position, mapped to FINISHED-VIDEO seconds through
OutputTimeline (North Star #2). The music bed and every voice-over take are followers.

What was wrong. The music preview computed the song position from RAW SOURCE seconds and
played at 1.0x beside a video running at the base speed (1.1x by default), with cuts skipped
and freezes held. It resynced only when the playhead jumped more than 0.5 s between ticks, so
during normal playback it drifted freely, and it disagreed with the export (which has always
placed music in output time, CUTS_02) wherever playback started. Voice-over takes tolerated
0.5 s of error on 300 ms of uncompensated buffering.

⚠️ THE MUSIC ALWAYS PLAYS AT ITS OWN NORMAL SPEED. Only the video speed changes. The music
player's "speed" is pinned to 1.0 on every start and is never adjusted; sync is corrected by
SEEKING the music to where the export will have it.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/MainWindow.PreviewMix.cs

### MainWindow — PREVIEWMIX_01, MUSICSYNC_02, PREVIEWMIX_02, VOPREVIEW_01, VOPRIO_01 (line 14)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
PREVIEWMIX_01 — THE PREVIEW PLAYS THE EXPORT'S OWN AUDIO.

The live preview is three independent players (gameplay, music bed, voice-over takes), so it
could never reproduce what only exists in the export's filter graph: the multiband ducking and
speech carving (the GAME is the music's sidechain), the voice-over protection, the peak tamer,
the safety limiter and the meme levels. Whenever the edit has any of those, the export's audio is
rendered in the background — ProcessWorker builds the export graph itself and AudioGraphPruner
runs only its audio half (measured: the rendered mix and the exported file's audio differ by
-60 dB RMS, i.e. AAC noise) — and played here in place of the live players, following the video
in output time exactly like the music bed does (seek-only correction, MUSICSYNC_02).

After every edit the old mix is dropped at once (the live players take over, so nothing stale is
ever heard) and a new one is rendered ~0.8 s after the edits stop.

PREVIEWMIX_02 — which mix may be heard is decided by ONE gate (`RenderedMixGate`): the
signature is re-observed on every playback tick BEFORE any preview audio is driven (not only on the
250 ms scheduler), every render is a numbered ticket that completes only if it is the newest and its
signature is still the edit's signature re-computed at completion, a WAV being overwritten stops
being a valid mix, and a failed render is latched instead of retried every 250 ms.

VOPREVIEW_01 — until a mix is ready (or when the edit has nothing the export would change), the
live players do what can be done live and exactly: the voice-over protection's 85% dip is a pure
time pulse (VOPRIO_01: voice first, then gameplay, then music), and the peak tamer is a static
filter on the gameplay player.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

PROJSESSION_06 — starts a fresh undo history for a newly loaded clip.

History does NOT survive a video change, deliberately. Every segment, cut and meme in the
stack is expressed in milliseconds into a specific file; undoing across a load would restore
positions that index into footage that is no longer open, and the result would be a timeline
that looks plausible and is wrong. A discarded history is recoverable by the user; a
silently mis-mapped one is not.

`gestureKey` coalesces a continuous gesture into one undo step. Pass the

appears not to work because each press moves the handle one pixel.

never happens — the window stays open and stays functional, rather than being hidden with
its work still in memory.

exported and saved, which produced three separate wrong behaviours:

  2. the same switch path wrote a fresh state file on the way out;
  3. the NEXT launch saw that state file, RecoveryManager.CheckFault() returned true, and the

Clearing the state file alone is enough to silence CheckFault (it early-returns when the file
is absent), but not enough on its own: SaveRecoveryState is wired to ~25 UI events and the
very next one would re-arm it, because HasUnsavedWork was still true. Hence this flag, which
HasUnsavedWork honours and which the first genuine edit clears.
