### MainWindow._memeScanGeneration — MEMECOMBO_01 (line 344)

MEMECOMBO_01 — monotonic scan generation. Only the NEWEST scan may write state.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE DEFECT THIS EXISTS TO CLOSE. `PopulateMemeComboBox` was `async void`
with no single-flight gate. It has at least three concurrent entry points — this.Loaded
(MainWindow.Wireup.cs), the STATIC MemeDirectory.Changed event (raised from SettingsWindow),
and RunCloudMemeSyncAsync after a download batch — and each returns to its caller at the
first await. Two overlapping invocations therefore both resumed, and whichever
ScanMemesAsync finished LAST won the write to _memeItems and to the ComboBox, regardless of
which was started last.

Because a scan's duration is proportional to library size, the SLOWER, OLDER scan reliably
won: the user changed the meme folder, the new folder's short scan landed first, and then
the old folder's long scan overwrote it. The combo then listed memes that were no longer in
the active directory, and picking one handed a stale FullPath straight into the export
payload.

_pendingMemeRestorePath made it worse. It is a read-null-write of shared state with no
ordering guarantee, so the FIRST invocation to resume consumed it — and if a later one won
the list write, the recovery-restore selection was silently dropped with no error anywhere.

A superseded scan now writes NOTHING: not _memeItems, not ItemsSource, not the restore path.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
CAPTIONWIPE_01 — EMPTIES THE TEXT STRIP'S CAPTION BETWEEN VIDEOS.

THE BUG THIS FIXES. The caption is a per-video TITLE, typed into PortraitTextInput and burnt
into the top strip of the finished portrait file. It was the only piece of the project that
survived both a finished export AND the loading of a different clip, so a session's second
video silently inherited the first one's title, the third inherited it again, and nothing on
screen flagged it — the box still showed the words, and a user who had already read them once
does not read them a second time. The mistake only surfaces in the exported file, after it has
been rendered and possibly uploaded.

WHEN IT RUNS. Both ends of the cycle, because either one alone leaves a hole:
  • after a SUCCESSFUL export (MainWindow.Export.cs) — that video is finished with;
  • when a different clip is loaded (`ResetEditingStateForNewVideo`) — covers
    the user who abandons a clip without exporting it, and the recovery-restore path that
    loads a clip straight into a fresh session.

It does NOT run on cancel or on a failed export: the user is still working on that video and
deleting their title would be its own small disaster.

ORDER MATTERS AT THE EXPORT CALL SITE. Writing OverlayText fires the ViewModel's
NotifyStateDirty, which re-arms the recovery state and clears ExportedCleanSinceLastEdit —
so this must be called BEFORE `_exportedCleanSinceLastEdit = true`, or a clean export would
immediately look dirty again and the crash-recovery prompt would be armed for a project that
is finished and saved.

Settings → Defaults → "Leave text from Video to Video" turns the whole thing off for people
who genuinely retype the same title every time; the flag ships OFF.

### MainWindow.ReturnToTrimStartPaused — ISSUE_06, RETURN_01 (line 1851)

Coalescing seek. At most one seek is in flight; anything requested while one is running is
remembered and issued when `OnSeekCompleted` fires.

===== ISSUE_06 — the "in flight" flag must only be raised if a seek is REALLY in flight ====
WHAT WAS WRONG: `_isSeeking = true` was set BEFORE the player was checked for null. The
only thing that ever clears that flag is the SeekCompleted callback, which the player
raises. So whenever there was no player — preview failed to start, GPU-less/RDP machine
where the fallback also failed, libmpv missing, or simply a seek attempted during teardown
— the flag was raised and NOTHING could ever lower it again. From that instant the
timeline slider, arrow-key frame stepping and every marker drag stopped moving the
playhead, silently, for the rest of the session: the user dragged the scrubber and nothing
happened, with no message anywhere.

The check now happens FIRST and the flag is only raised once the command has actually been
handed to the player. The try/catch is the matching guarantee for the other direction: if
the command throws, the flag comes back down instead of wedging the timeline.

RETURN_01 — park the preview at MARK START, paused, after any sub-editor closes.

Coming back from the Granular editor, the Voice Over studio or the Music Wizard, the
playhead was left wherever that window had wandered to — in practice the MARK END position,
i.e. the very end of the clip. The user has just changed something and wants to watch it
back, and the one thing they cannot do from the end is press play. Parking at the trim
START with playback paused means the next click reviews the edit that was just made.

Pause FIRST, then seek: seeking a playing clip lets it run on from the new position, which
would immediately undo the parking.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
EDIT3_02 — "REMOVE SPEEDS" IS NOW "EDIT SPEEDS", AND IT IS NO LONGER RED.

The red button was honest when the button really did wipe everything on one click. It stopped
being honest the moment EDIT3_01 put a chooser in front of it: the button's job is now
"open the thing you already made", and removing is one of three answers inside. A red button

### MainWindow.ConfirmToolSwitchAsync — SWITCHPROMPT_01 (line 2495)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SWITCHPROMPT_01 — ASKS BEFORE LEAVING FOR A COMPANION TOOL, BUT ONLY WHEN THERE IS SOMETHING
TO LOSE.

THE BUG. `AppSettings.ConfirmMainAppSwitchTool` has existed, been surfaced in Settings,
and been loaded and saved for a long time — and NOTHING EVER READ IT. Both switch paths
(the VIDEO MERGER / CROP SETTINGS buttons and their Tools-menu twins) called
`SwitchToCompanionAppAsync` directly. Whatever prompt the user was seeing could
therefore not be turned off from Settings and could not tell an empty editor from a full
one: it fired with no video loaded at all, warning about losing work that did not exist.
A warning that appears when nothing is at stake is worse than no warning, because it teaches
the user to dismiss the one that matters.

THE RULE. Two conditions, both required:
  1. the user has left the setting on, AND
  2. `HasUnsavedWork` is true.

HasUnsavedWork is already exactly the right predicate and says so in its own summary:
"A LOADED VIDEO IS NOT WORK. Uploading a clip and touching nothing else must return false —
that is exactly the case the Video Merger / Crop Tools switch prompt must NOT interrupt."
It returns true only for a real edit: a start or end mark, a thumbnail, a cut, a speed
segment or changed base speed, a freeze, granular speed, music, a voice-over, a meme, a HUD
toggle, a changed export toggle, or typed caption text. Loading a clip and looking at it is
none of those, and neither is scrubbing, playing or changing the volume.

Returns TRUE when the caller should go ahead.

app's default speed is 1.1 (`SpeedPresetButtons.NativeDefaultSpeed`). |1.1-1.0| = 0.1,
so the condition was TRUE from the instant the window opened, for every user on the
defaults — permanently. Two opposite failures came out of that one wrong constant: the
ClearState() branch in SaveRecoveryState was effectively dead, so a stale recovery file
lingered after the user removed their last edit; and the moment anyone chose exactly 1.0x —
an entirely normal choice — the test flipped to false and the file was DELETED, taking
everything in RECOVERY_04 with it. Compare against the real default, so this means what it
says.

RECOVERY_04: the meme choice and the HUD/portrait toggles are all written into the recovery
payload, yet none of them used to count as "work". If they were the user's only edits the
app decided there was nothing to keep and ERASED the file — and since the toggle handlers
call SaveRecoveryState() on every click, changing a HUD toggle actively destroyed the recovery
state instead of saving it. They are counted here.
⚠️ These two fixes are a PAIR. RECOVERY_03 alone would have exposed RECOVERY_04 immediately;
RECOVERY_04 alone leaves the dead-branch half of RECOVERY_03 in place.

⚠️ A LOADED VIDEO IS NOT WORK. Uploading a clip and touching nothing else must return false —
that is exactly the case the Video Merger / Crop Tools switch prompt must NOT interrupt.
Do not add "_videoPath != null" to this expression.

### MemeCatalog.ScanAsync — MEMESCAN_01 (line 98)

§1 File Ingestion: scans the ACTIVE meme directory for supported formats, skipping
zero-byte files, and resolves each file's native dimensions (ffprobe for videos,
SkiaSharp for images). Runs fully off the UI thread.
§3 Exception Handling: UnauthorizedAccessException propagates so the Settings flow
can block the path change and revert; all other per-file errors are swallowed.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
MEMESCAN_01 — WHY THIS IS THREE PHASES INSTEAD OF ONE LOOP.

WHAT WAS WRONG: a single foreach spawned ONE ffprobe child process per video, STRICTLY
SERIALLY, via `new MediaProber(...).GetResolutionAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult()`.
Three separate costs compounded:

  1. Serial process launches. ~100 ms each on Windows (CreateProcess + image load + ffprobe's
     own demuxer probe), and a single unreadable or network-backed file cost the full
     15-second MediaProber timeout on its own, blocking every file behind it.
  2. No memoisation, despite MediaProber having some. A NEW MediaProber was constructed
     inside the loop body and dropped on the next iteration, so its SemaphoreSlim-guarded
     _probeData cache never served a single hit on this path.
  3. Sync-over-async inside Task.Run. .GetAwaiter().GetResult() parks a thread-pool worker
     for the whole probe. The pool injects roughly one thread per 500 ms, so a large scan
     starved every other queued Task.Run in the app — filmstrip prewarm, size estimation,
     loudness probes — behind it.

And this path is re-entered on window Loaded (cold start), on every MemeDirectory.Changed,
and immediately after a cloud sync — i.e. right when the library is at its largest.

THE FIX: enumerate cheaply, resolve dimensions from a persisted (length, mtime)-keyed cache
and probe only the misses under a bounded worker pool with real awaits, then assemble.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### MemeCatalog.SyncFolderAsync — ISSUE_11, MEMESYNC_01, MEMESYNC_03, MEMESYNC_02 (line 334)

Shared delta-sync engine.

ISSUE_11 — progress (the listing is enumerated FIRST so a real total is known), cancellation
(a cancelled transfer leaves no partial file behind), and distinct error messages.

MEMESYNC_01 — WHY THE LISTING USES THE GIT TREES API AND NOT /contents.
The contents API returns at most 1,000 entries per folder and has no paging, so a library
past 1,000 files silently stopped growing. `git/trees/HEAD:{folder}` returns up to 100,000
entries in one call (and says so with `truncated` beyond that), and it reports each blob's
SIZE, which MEMESYNC_03 below depends on.

MEMESYNC_02 — A MISSING FOLDER IS AN ERROR, NOT "NOTHING NEW". A 404 on the listing used to
be logged and skipped, so the sync reported zero files to fetch and the UI said "You already
have everything" — a false statement the user had no way to see through. Any listing failure
now returns an error message.

MEMESYNC_03 — LFS FILES GO STRAIGHT TO THE LFS HOST. Media is Git-LFS tracked, so a raw
download of it returns a ~130-byte pointer file. The old engine downloaded that pointer
first, noticed, and then downloaded the real file — two requests per file. A blob whose
listed size is at most `LfsPointerMaxBytes` is a pointer, so its first request
goes to media.githubusercontent.com. The other host stays as the fallback, because
media.githubusercontent.com answers 404 for a file that is NOT in LFS.

### MemeCatalog.LfsPointerMaxBytes — MEMESYNC_03 (line 528)

MEMESYNC_03 — a Git-LFS pointer file is ~130 bytes; anything this small is one.

MEMESYNC_03 — one attempt against one host. True only when `tmp` now holds
real, non-empty content (not an LFS pointer). A 404 is a normal "not on this host" answer.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/MpvVideoView.cs

### MpvVideoView.ImportedImageSlot — GPUSLOT_01 (line 62)

GPUSLOT_01 — one imported GPU image plus the generation stamp that identifies it.

The generation is what makes a stale UI-thread completion callback harmless: the callback
compares the slot it was handed against the slot that is there NOW, and if they differ it
knows a newer import has already replaced it and does nothing.

### MpvVideoView._importedImages — GPUSLOT_01 (line 81)

GPUSLOT_01 — THE SWAP-CHAIN SLOTS. READ AND WRITTEN BY THREE THREADS. NEVER TOUCH AN ELEMENT
WITH A BARE ARRAY ASSIGNMENT.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
WHAT WAS WRONG: this was a plain ICompositionImportedGpuImage?[] with no lock, no volatile
and no Interlocked, and it was written from three places on three different threads:

  • the RENDER thread, in EnsureImportedImage (import / replace a lost image),
  • the UI thread, inside ImportAndPresentTexture's fire-and-forget continuation, which on a
    failed present disposed "whatever is in the slot" and nulled it,
  • the teardown path (OnDetachedFromVisualTree / ReleaseRenderTexture).

The catch blocks did not dispose the `image` they had actually failed on — they disposed
_importedImages[index], which by that point could be a DIFFERENT, newly imported object. So a
failed present could destroy the live image the render thread was about to draw with, and the
render thread could hand a freshly disposed import to UpdateWithKeyedMutexAsync. That is a
use-after-dispose across a COM boundary on the hot path, and the silent swallow of
COMException 0x80070057 (E_INVALIDARG) further down was the field evidence of it.

THE RULE NOW:
  • The RENDER thread is the sole importer and the sole publisher (Interlocked.Exchange).
  • The UI thread is a pure observer. It may only remove a slot with
    Interlocked.CompareExchange against the EXACT slot it was given, and may dispose only if
    that CompareExchange proves the slot is still the one it failed on.
  • Teardown claims slots with Interlocked.Exchange too.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### MpvVideoView._imageGeneration — GPUSLOT_01 (line 111)

GPUSLOT_01 — monotonic stamp; every successful import takes the next value.

### MpvVideoView._presentGates — GPUPRESENT_01, ZOOMHANG_01 (line 114)

GPUPRESENT_01 — one permit per swap-chain slot, so at most ONE UpdateWithKeyedMutexAsync is
ever in flight for a given slot.

ImportAndPresentTexture posts to the UI thread and does NOT await the result, so the render
thread could issue present N+1 for a slot while present N was still running. Two overlapping
UpdateWithKeyedMutexAsync calls on the SAME IDXGIKeyedMutex with the same
(ConsumerKey, ProducerKey) pair produce an unordered AcquireSync/ReleaseSync sequence, and an
AcquireSync for a key no producer will release is an UNBOUNDED BLOCK — on the UI thread. That
is the one deadlock ZOOMHANG_01's render-thread timeout cannot save you from, because it is
the UI thread that stops.

A frame that cannot take its slot's permit promptly is DROPPED, not queued: at 60fps the next
one is 16ms away and a queue here is latency the user sees as lag.

freed unless every worker was accounted for, so a failed attempt is retryable.

defensive backstop, not the correctness argument). Frees each native resource exactly once
in the documented order and reports the outcome to the caller.

### MpvVideoView.TryAcquireProducerKey — GPUPRESENT_02 (line 2192)

GPUPRESENT_02 — acquire the producer key for a slot whose present permit the caller HOLDS.

Holding the permit proves no UpdateWithKeyedMutexAsync is in flight for this slot. So a
texture found on ConsumerKey is an orphan: a present failed, or was never posted, before the
compositor acquired it. It is reclaimed (AcquireSync(ConsumerKey, 0) + ReleaseSync(ProducerKey))
instead of waiting for a consumer that will never come. Render thread only, _renderLock held.

NON-BLOCKING GUARANTEE: Never blocks for 1000ms while holding _renderLock. If the slot is
still being sampled by the compositor, it returns false immediately (0ms) so the search
loop can test the remaining slots in the 16-slot ring.

### MpvVideoView.PumpEmptyRender — ISSUE_05 (line 2251)

ISSUE_05 — this method used to have a COMPLETELY EMPTY BODY while its name promised the
opposite, and every "cannot draw this frame" branch in `UpdateSurface` called
it and returned.

WHY THAT FROZE THE PREVIEW: with `vo=libmpv` mpv hands the client one frame and then
WAITS — it only decodes and announces the next frame once the current one has been
consumed by a call to `mpv_render_context_render`. So declining to render (surface
not created yet, control not laid out, or the 1-second keyed-mutex acquire timing out
under load) meant: no render -> no new frame -> no new frame-ready callback -> the
picture stays frozen on one image for the rest of the session while the audio plays on.
Restarting the app was the only way out.

THE FIX: consume the frame with `MPV_RENDER_PARAM_SKIP_RENDERING=1`. mpv does all the
timing/frame-advance bookkeeping and skips only the draw, so the clock keeps moving and
the very next frame is offered normally. It does not touch the graphics API, so this is
safe to call with no GL context current — which matters, because these branches are
reached precisely when the GL/D3D side is not usable.

FAIL-SAFE: any failure is swallowed. The bounded 66ms wait in `RenderThreadLoop`
is the second, independent line of defence — even if this pump never works on some driver,
the loop still retries ~15x/sec, so the preview recovers either way.

GPUSLOT_01 — render thread only. The sole importer and the sole publisher for a slot.
Returns the slot (image + generation) rather than a bare image, because the present path must
be able to prove later that the slot has not been replaced underneath it.

GPUSLOT_01 — the single disposal funnel. Imported GPU images belong to the compositor, so the
release is posted to the UI thread; every call site goes through here so there is exactly one
place that can destroy one.

GPUSLOT_01 — remove a slot ONLY if it is still the exact slot the caller was working with.

GPUSLOT_01 / GPUPRESENT_01 / GPUPRESENT_02 — hand one slot's image to the compositor.

Takes the SLOT, not a bare image, so the completion callback can prove the slot is still the
one it was given before it destroys anything.
⚠️ GPUPRESENT_02: the caller has ALREADY taken this slot's present permit (UpdateSurface takes
it before AcquireSync). This method owns releasing it on every path. A failed present
leaves the texture on ConsumerKey. That is safe now, because the next producer to take the
permit reclaims it (TryAcquireProducerKey) instead of timing out on it.

MPVSHUTDOWN_01 — the SYNCHRONOUS teardown is the PROCESS-FINAL FALLBACK ONLY. Every
interactive UI path (tool navigation, window close) uses `ShutdownAsync`, whose
waits are asynchronous. This body may still join threads and try locks with bounds because
its callers are immediately followed by Environment.Exit — the one case where a bounded
block cannot strand the user. If an async shutdown is already in flight, it is observed
first so the two paths can never free the same native handles.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/MusicWizardResult.Plan.cs

### MusicWizardResult — MUSICWIN_01 (line 7)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
MUSICWIN_01 — EVERY SONG'S CHOSEN PART, AND ONE WAY TO READ IT.

The Add Music wizard now lets the user choose which part of EVERY song plays (drag the song's
edges on the Fit & Mix screen), not only where the first song starts. Those choices travel
in `MusicStartsSeconds` / `MusicEndsSeconds`, index-aligned with
`MusicWizardResult.MusicFilePaths`.

The Main App export, the Main App preview, the Video Merger export and the Video Merger preview
each used to rebuild "paths + durations + first offset" by hand, and each filtered missing files
and then indexed the durations by the FILTERED position — so one missing song shifted every
length after it onto the wrong file. `ToBedTracks` is the one reader now: it keeps
the original index for every lookup and only then drops missing files.

Older results (and saved sessions) carry no windows: the first song then starts at
`MusicWizardResult.OffsetSeconds`, every other song at 0, and every song plays to
its end — exactly the layout they were saved with.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/MusicWizardWindow.Controls.cs

### MusicWizardWindow — MVVM_03, MVVM_02, QUALITY_04, MVVM_01 (line 11)

MVVM_03 — the cached control accessors for `MusicWizardWindow`.

⚠️ IN ITS OWN FILE ON PURPOSE. MVVM_02 caps window code-behind and the cap may only ever
fall, so adding these to the code-behind — even while REMOVING lookups from it — would
have pushed several files past their ceiling and forced the ratchet up. A ratchet that
gets raised to accommodate an improvement stops being a ratchet.

These replace repeated `this.FindControl<T>("Name")` calls — some controls were
resolved by string fifteen times in one file. Each lookup walks the visual tree and can
return null, so a renamed control compiled cleanly and produced a dead button at run time
(QUALITY_04). Now a rename breaks in exactly one place.

This is a STEP toward MVVM_01, not the destination. The end state is a binding to a
view-model property; until then, one resolution per control means the eventual binding
replaces one accessor instead of hunting every call site.

One ordered list of songs, each with the part of it that plays (`MusicPlaylistEntry`),
replaces the old "one song + auto-fill queue of whole files". Everything the wizard shows about

    first song when NEXT is pressed.
  • "Fill the rest automatically" adds songs from the visible list, in its order, until the video
    is covered.

SILENCETRIM_01 — each added song is analysed in the background and, unless the user already
moved its edges, its silent intro and outro are trimmed off, so two songs never leave dead air
between them.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SONGLANE_01 + SONGCARD_01 — WHERE EACH SONG PLAYS, AND WHICH PART OF IT.

SONGLANE_01 — the music lane under the film shows one coloured, numbered, named block per song,
at the exact place it plays in the finished video (the plan's output seconds), and a red
"no music" band over any part of the video the songs do not reach. The right edge of every
block can be dragged: it is where that song ENDS. Shortening a song pulls every later song
earlier — songs always follow each other with the export's crossfade, never with a gap. Clicking
a block picks that song for the song card and moves the playhead there.

SONGCARD_01 — the song card draws the picked song WHOLE, with the part that plays lit up:
  • drag inside the bright box → a different part of the song plays (same length);
  • drag the box's left / right edge → trim the start / the end;
  • click outside the box → the box starts there;
  • on release, "Snap to beat" moves the start onto the nearest strong beat.
A dashed line inside the box marks where the video ends when the song is cut short by it.

Both read `CurrentPlan`, so what is drawn is what is heard and what is exported.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### MusicWizardWindow._phase3Cuts — CUTS_02, TIME_01 (line 468)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
CUTS_02 — SECTIONS THE SPEED EDITOR DELETED, in absolute source milliseconds.

This wizard lays music against the length of the FINISHED video. Every duration it works
from — the coverage check, Smart Fit's search window, Fit By End Of Video, the phase-3
timeline, the result's TimelineEndSeconds — comes out of
CalculatePhase3EffectiveDurationSeconds, and that was building its OutputTimeline without
the cuts. So a project with two minutes deleted told the wizard the video was two minutes
longer than it will be: the music was stretched to cover footage that no longer exists, and
every beat aligned by Smart Fit landed two minutes off the mark.

This is the identical class of bug as TIME_01 (freezes making the video longer than this
method believed) and is fixed the same way: hand the real edit list to the one type that
owns source-to-output time, and let it do the arithmetic.

Nothing is DRAWN for these. Phase 3's timeline is output time, where a cut is zero seconds
wide by definition — there is no gap to mark, because in the finished video there is none.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### MusicWizardWindow._phase3Memes — MEME_06, CUTS_03, TIME_01 (line 490)

MEME_06 — memes spliced into the video, in clip-relative source seconds.

Same class of bug as CUTS_03 and TIME_01, from the opposite direction: a cut makes the
finished video SHORTER than this wizard believed, a meme makes it LONGER. Without these the
coverage check, Smart Fit, Fit By End Of Video and the phase-3 preview would all lay music
against a video shorter than the one that gets exported, so the music would stop early by
the total length of every meme.

Nothing is drawn for them here: phase 3's ruler is output time, where a meme is a stretch of
foreign footage the music simply plays over (or not — see KeepMusicDuringMeme).

### MusicWizardWindow.CalculatePhase3EffectiveDurationSeconds — TIME_01 (line 2582)

TIME_01 - how long phase 3's video actually runs for once speed changes and freezes have
stretched it.

THIS METHOD USED TO BE WRONG. Its hand-written loop advanced its cursor past a freeze
(`cursor = Math.Max(cursor, segEnd)`), i.e. it believed a held frame REPLACED the footage
underneath it. The exported graph does the opposite - `GranularSpeedBuilder` holds the frame
and then carries on playing from the same spot, so a 1.5 second freeze makes the finished
video 1.5 seconds LONGER and skips nothing. Measured against the export as ground truth this
method under-reported by the whole freeze duration every time: 63.000s reported as 60.000s
for a single 3 second freeze, 33.000s as 31.500s at base speed 2x. Music was therefore
positioned against a length the finished video never had.

It now delegates to `FreeVideoStudio.Core.Media.OutputTimeline`, the single
shared model, so it cannot disagree with the export again.

### MusicWizardWindow.MapPhase3OutputToSourceRelativeSeconds — TIME_01, CUTS_03 (line 2613)

TIME_01 - a moment in the FINISHED video to the source moment showing at that instant,
measured from the trim-in point.

Carried the same freeze error as `CalculatePhase3EffectiveDurationSeconds` and is
fixed the same way, by delegating to the shared
`FreeVideoStudio.Core.Media.OutputTimeline`. Inside a held frame the answer
is deliberately lossy - every moment of the freeze shows the same source instant, so that
instant is what comes back.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
CUTS_03 — WHY PHASE 3 NEEDS NO SKIP LOOP OF ITS OWN.

This preview is driven from an OUTPUT clock: the wizard counts finished-video seconds and
asks this method where in the source footage that moment lives, then seeks mpv there. A cut
occupies zero output time, so once the timeline knows about it, no output second can ever
map into deleted footage — the deleted span is simply never a possible answer, and the
preview steps over it on its own.

Which is exactly why the missing argument here was so quiet: the timeline was built WITHOUT
the cuts, so it still believed every deleted second was playable, mapped output seconds
into them, and told mpv to go and show the user footage that will not be in their video.
The fix is the cut list, not a watchdog.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ISSUE_09 — THIS WAS 95 LINES OF HAND-ROLLED TOAST. IT IS NOW ONE LINE.

The old body built a Border by hand, hunted for `Step1Panel`'s parent to host it, computed a
ZIndex from its siblings, then hand-animated opacity in a `for` loop with `await Task.Delay(16)`
— twice. It slid in from the TOP of the wizard while every other screen in the suite put its
feedback somewhere else entirely, and it had TWO early `return`s (one if `Step1Panel` was not
found, one if its parent was not a Panel) that made the message vanish silently rather than
show up somewhere imperfect. A user who pressed a button and saw nothing had no way to tell a
no-op from a lost message.

Every one of the 13 call sites is unchanged — they still call ShowToast(text). What changed is
that they now produce the SAME float-up-and-fade notice as the Main App, the Speed Editor, the
Merger, the Crop Tools and the Voice Over recorder.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/PreviewDetachController.cs

### PreviewDetachController — DETACH_01 (line 10)

DETACH_01 — ONE implementation of "pop the video preview out into its own window", shared by
every screen in the suite that shows a live preview.

The Main App had this behaviour and nothing else did. Rather than copy the reparenting dance
into the Granular editor, the Music Wizard, the Voice Over window and the Merger — four more
places to get the teardown order wrong — the whole mechanism lives here and each window
supplies only two things:

  • a BOUNDS KEY, which is what gives every screen its OWN memory of size, position, maximised
    state and therefore which physical display it was last opened on. They are deliberately
    separate keys: detaching the Granular preview onto the second monitor must not drag the
    Main App's preview there next time.
  • a CONTENT ACCESSOR returning the control to move. Usually the `MpvVideoView`
    itself, but the Granular editor hands over its whole Viewbox so the zoom overlay and the
    phone frame travel WITH the picture and stay in register with it.

⚠️ THE ORIGIN IS CAPTURED, NOT ASSUMED. The Main App's original version hard-coded
"put it back into MainVideoGrid at index 0" on reattach. That only worked because it was the
only caller. This records the actual parent — Panel (with its child index), Decorator or
ContentControl — and restores exactly that, so a preview nested behind other overlays comes
back in the same z-order it left from.

⚠️ THE OWNER'S Closing REATTACHES FIRST. A detached preview is a live mpv render surface
parented to a different window. If the owner closed while it was still out there, the surface
would be torn down by whichever window happened to die first. Reattaching on the owner's
Closing puts it back in its home tree so the owner's normal disposal path runs unchanged.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/PreviewShutdown.cs

### PreviewShutdownStatus — MPVSHUTDOWN_01 (line 9)

Outcome of a preview teardown request (MPVSHUTDOWN_01).

### PreviewShutdownStatus.Succeeded (line 12)

Every worker stopped and every native resource was released, exactly once.

### PreviewShutdownStatus.AlreadyStopped (line 14)

Nothing left to do: this stack was already torn down (idempotent re-request).

### PreviewShutdownStatus.FailedWorkerDidNotStop (line 16)

Phase A timed out: a render/software worker did not acknowledge shutdown in time.
NOTHING was freed; the caller must NOT build a replacement preview stack.

### PreviewShutdownStatus.Failed (line 19)

Teardown was cancelled or failed during/after quiescence. Nothing was freed unless
the status says so; the caller must NOT build a replacement preview stack.

### PreviewShutdownResult — MPVSHUTDOWN_01 (line 24)

MPVSHUTDOWN_01 — the awaitable completion contract of a preview teardown.

A failed teardown is a RESULT, never an exception and never a silent "best effort": the caller
(ToolNavigator, window close paths) must be able to tell "the GPU stack is provably gone" from
"something may still be alive", because only the first makes creating a replacement
`MpvVideoView` safe in this long-lived process.

### PreviewShutdownResult.Succeeded (line 36)

True only when the native stack is provably released (or was never there).

### PreviewShutdownCoordinator — MPVSHUTDOWN_01 (line 45)

MPVSHUTDOWN_01 — the two halves of preview shutdown as pure, testable logic.

**Idempotency:** `RunAsync` returns the SAME in-flight operation to every caller;
a second call after a successful one returns `PreviewShutdownResult.AlreadyStopped`.
Stop signals are therefore never sent twice and no cleanup workflow runs twice.

**Phase A — quiescence:** `QuiesceAsync` awaits worker completion tasks with a
bounded `Task.WhenAny`. There is no `Thread.Join` anywhere: waiting is
asynchronous, and the UI thread is never the thread that blocks.

### PreviewShutdownCoordinator.Pending (line 66)

The in-flight shutdown, for the synchronous process-final fallback to observe. Null when idle.

### PreviewShutdownCoordinator.MarkCompleted (line 69)

Marks the stack released (called by the synchronous process-exit path after a full cleanup).

### PreviewShutdownCoordinator.RunAsync (line 72)

Runs (or attaches to) the one shutdown workflow this coordinator will ever have in flight.
`core` performs the actual two-phase teardown; it may be invoked more than
once across separate calls ONLY after a FAILED attempt (retrying a failed teardown is safe —
signalling is idempotent and nothing was freed), never after a successful one.

### PreviewShutdownCoordinator.QuiesceAsync — MPVSHUTDOWN_01 (line 122)

MPVSHUTDOWN_01 — PHASE A. Awaits proof that every worker stopped, in bounded time.
Completed/never-started workers (null entries) do not count against the timeout.

### PreviewShutdownCoordinator.QuiescePresentGatesAsync — VOAPPLY_05 (line 146)

VOAPPLY_05 / UI-GPUPRESENT2 — Awaits quiescence of swap-chain presentation gates.
Acquiring each permit proves the compositor has completed updating the corresponding slot.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/RuntimeLog.cs

### RuntimeLog.MaxSingleEntryBytes (line 22)

ISSUE_1 — hard ceiling on ONE log entry.

Without this the 10 MB file cap is not enforceable: a single caller can hand the queue an
arbitrarily large string (the biggest real one today is the 400-line FFmpeg stderr dump in
ProcessWorker, roughly 40 KB), and one entry larger than MaxLogSize would blow the cap the
instant it is written to a freshly rotated, empty file. Oversized entries are truncated
with an explicit marker rather than dropped, so evidence is never silently lost.

### RuntimeLog.MaxBatchBytes (line 33)

ISSUE_1 — hard ceiling on ONE write batch.

The drain loop used to empty the ENTIRE queue (up to 10,000 entries) into one StringBuilder
before the size check ran, so the batch itself was unbounded in both memory and bytes
written. Bounding the batch is what makes the "rotate before the cap is exceeded" check
meaningful: after a rotation the new file receives at most this much.

### RuntimeLog.EmergencyWrite (line 315)

Synchronous, queue-BYPASSING, best-effort direct write to the log file, flushed to
disk immediately. Crash handlers must use this: a native access violation (0xC0000005)
fast-fails the process before the async `ProcessLogQueue` can drain, so a
normal Info/Fail would never reach disk. This writes straight through so the crash line
survives the process dying. Uses the pre-resolved cached path to avoid taking locks in
a possibly-corrupted process state.

named by a SHA-256 of the caller's key (the key holds file identity + company + model, never an API key).

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Services/AiHudFrameBuilder.cs

### AiHudFrameBuilder — AIHUD_01 (line 11)

AIHUD_01 — turns the Crop Tool's ONE frozen snapshot into the `AiHudFrame` an AI
provider is allowed to see. No UI types; call it off the UI thread.

**Only this frame.** The input is the snapshot file the user is looking at — the same
pixels the source canvas shows. The video file is touched only for its size and timestamp, to
fingerprint it; its contents are never read here and never sent.

**Size.** The JPEG is downscaled so its long edge is at most `MaxLongEdge`.
The AI answers in normalized 0..1 coordinates, so downscaling cannot shift a box; the mapping
back to pixels uses the SOURCE dimensions, never the JPEG's.

**Identity.** `AiHudFrame.FrameKey` is a hash of the snapshot's own bytes,
so two different frames can never share a cached answer. `AiHudFrame.SourceFingerprint`
is a hash of the clip's full path, length and write time — opaque, no path text.

### AiHudFrameBuilder.SourceFingerprint (line 78)

Opaque clip identity: hash of full path + length + last write (UTC ticks). No path text leaves.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Services/AiJsonSchema.cs

### AiJsonSchema — AISCHEMA_01 (line 10)

AISCHEMA_01 (docs/05 SYS-AISETTINGS) — one translator from the app's response schemas (written in
Google's OpenAPI dialect: upper-case types, `nullable`, array roots) to the JSON Schema the other
vendors accept, and back again for the answer.

- Types are lower-cased; `nullable: true` becomes a `[type, "null"]` union.
- Claude tools and OpenAI structured outputs both require an OBJECT root, so an array root is
wrapped as `{ "items": [...] }` and unwrapped from the answer (`Normalize`).
- OpenAI strict mode (`strict`) also requires `additionalProperties: false`
on every object and every property listed in `required`; optional properties become nullable,
and `Normalize` drops the resulting `null` values so callers see "missing" exactly
as they do from Gemini.

### AiJsonSchema.WrapProperty (line 26)

The property an array-root schema is wrapped in.

### AiJsonSchema.Translate (line 31)

Translates `schema` for Claude (`strict` = false) or OpenAI (true).
Empty or unreadable input is returned unchanged.

### AiJsonSchema.Normalize (line 73)

Turns a vendor's answer back into what the Gemini path would have produced: strips a code fence,
unwraps `WrapProperty` when the schema was wrapped (a bare array is accepted too), and
removes `null`-valued object properties. Unreadable text is returned fence-stripped, unchanged,
so the caller's own parser reports it.

### AiJsonSchema.ToGeminiDialect — AISCHEMA_02 (line 102)

AISCHEMA_02 — the reverse direction for Gemini: features written in standard JSON Schema (lower-case
types, e.g. Music Auto-Fit, Viral Post, Kill Tracker) are sent to Gemini with UPPER-CASE type names,
the dialect its `responseSchema` documents. Already-Gemini schemas pass through unchanged.
Unreadable input is returned unchanged.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Services/AuthenticodeVerifier.cs

### AuthenticodeVerifier — UPDATETRUST_01, UPDATETRUST_02, SIGNMANDATE_01 (line 11)

UPDATETRUST_01 — Authenticode verification for a file this process is about to EXECUTE.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
WHY THIS EXISTS. `UpdateService` downloaded an .exe, checked its SHA-256 against a digest
read out of the SAME GitHub JSON document that supplied the download URL, and then launched it
with `--install --auto-update` and `UseShellExecute = true` — i.e. elevated, with the
"preserve your settings?" question force-answered YES.

That hash proves TRANSPORT INTEGRITY and nothing else: it proves the bytes match what that JSON
claimed, not that we published them. Anyone able to produce that response body — a compromised
repo or CI token, a TLS-terminating corporate proxy, a mis-issued certificate — controls the
payload AND the fingerprint that validates it, in one move. The end state is attacker-supplied
code running as Administrator behind a single UAC click.

The verification primitive already existed on the OTHER side of the pipe: `build/FvsBuild/
CodeSigning.cs` Authenticode-signs the shipped binary and then runs `signtool verify /pa`
over it. Nothing on the RECEIVING side ever looked. This class is that missing half.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

**THE TRUST ANCHOR IS THE RUNNING PROCESS, NOT A HARDCODED THUMBPRINT.** A constant baked
into the source goes stale the day the signing certificate is renewed, and a stale pin fails
CLOSED — it would silently kill auto-update for every existing install until they manually
reinstalled. Instead the currently running executable is the anchor: it is already on the user's
disk, they already chose to run it, and it carries the publisher identity we want to stay with.
An update is accepted only when it is Authenticode-valid AND signed by the same publisher
subject as the binary asking for it.

**⚠️ UNSIGNED BUILDS — UPDATETRUST_02.** When the running process is itself unsigned there
is no anchor to compare against, so `EvaluateUpdateCandidate` returns
`TrustVerdict.NoAnchor`.

**That verdict is now a REFUSAL at the call site, not a fall-through.** It previously
degraded to hash-only "so nothing regresses for an unsigned distribution" — but the unsigned
distribution WAS production (see SIGNMANDATE_01 in `build/FvsBuild/CodeSigning.cs`), so the
degraded path was the only path that ever ran and the attack described at the top of this file
was never actually closed. `UpdateService` now deletes the download and tells the user to
install the signed build once by hand. `FVS_ALLOW_UNSIGNED_UPDATE=1` restores the old
behaviour for developers only.

This class's verdict is unchanged and deliberately stays a three-way classification rather than
a bool: WHAT to do about a missing anchor is policy, and policy belongs with the caller that
owns the consequence, not with the primitive that reads the signature.

**Revocation is deliberately NOT checked** (`WTD_REVOKE_NONE`). A revocation lookup
needs network at exactly the moment the machine may have none left, and an offline CRL/OCSP
fetch fails in a way indistinguishable from a real revocation — which would reject legitimate
updates for offline users. Publisher pinning against the running binary is the stronger control
here: defeating it requires our actual signing key, which revocation would not have helped with
in the window before it was noticed.

The outcome of evaluating a downloaded file against the running process.

### AuthenticodeVerifier.TrustVerdict.Trusted (line 80)

### AuthenticodeVerifier.TrustVerdict.NoAnchor (line 83)

The ANCHOR is unsigned, so no publisher comparison is possible. Caller decides.

SIGNPATH_01 — the free open-source signing certificate. Its publisher is "SignPath Foundation",
which signs MANY open-source programs, so its name proves nothing about which program a file is.
A file signed with it is trusted only when (1) Windows fully trusts the signature (public root,
intact, chain valid) AND (2) its SHA-256 equals the hash in the update list that the Free Video
Studio publisher root signed (`listedSha256`, UPDATEPIN_01 / DIST-SMART). The
list stays the proof of WHICH file; the public signature only satisfies Windows. This is what lets
copies signed with the repository certificate install the first SignPath-signed release, and
stops "same publisher name" from being enough between two SignPath-signed files.

The VERIFY call must always be paired with a CLOSE call or the provider leaks its state.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Services/DiagnosticBundle.cs

### DiagnosticBundle — FAULTTIER_01 (line 12)

SYS-DIAGREPORT — COLLECTS THE DIAGNOSTIC BUNDLE AND PUTS IT SOMEWHERE THE USER CAN FIND IT.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
**THE GAP THIS FILLS.** `FAULTTIER_01` classifies every failure and routes it to a log.
The Fatal tier even shows the user the log's path. But the path is to a rotating file under
`%ProgramData%\Free Video Studio\logs`, and the number of users who will navigate
there, identify the right file among the rotation, and attach it to a report is approximately
zero. So the fault tiers made failures VISIBLE to the user and left them invisible to whoever
has to fix them.

⚠️ THE PRODUCT'S CENTRAL RISK IS HARDWARE IT HAS NEVER RUN ON. `HardwareScanner` chooses
between NVENC, AMF, QSV and d3d11va at runtime against a matrix tested on one machine. Without
this, a GPU-specific export failure arrives as "it doesn't work on my PC" and stays there.

**NOTHING HERE UPLOADS ANYTHING.** It writes a plain-text file and hands back the path. The
user reads it, decides, and sends it — or does not. Silent telemetry from a video editor would
be an unpleasant surprise in a product whose users are recording their own screens, and a
consent dialog nobody understands is not better. A readable file is the honest version.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### DiagnosticBundle.FolderFor (line 41)

Where bundles are written. One folder so the user is told one place to look.

### DiagnosticBundle.WriteAsync (line 48)

SYS-DIAGREPORT — builds the bundle and writes it.

Runs entirely on a worker: it reads log files that can be megabytes and probes the encoder,
and Invariant #6 forbids the UI dispatcher blocking on either. The caller awaits and then
shows the path.

**detectedEncoder:**
What `HardwareScanner` settled on, when it has run. Passed in rather than probed here:
re-probing would report what the hardware can do NOW, and the useful answer is what the
failing session actually chose.

**Returns:** The path written, or `null` when nothing could be written.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Services/ExportCoordinator.cs

### ExportCoordinator — EXPORTSESSION_02, EXPORTSESSION_01, CANCELREG_01 (line 8)

EXPORTSESSION_02 — the export lifecycle, moved out of MainWindow so it can be tested without a
window (EXPORTSESSION_01's guarantees, unchanged, now owned here).

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE RULES CARRIED OVER FROM EXPORTSESSION_01, AND WHERE EACH ONE LIVES NOW:

  • One export at a time. `StartAsync` rejects while Running OR Cancelling — the
    Cancelling window is the one the old processButton.IsEnabled "lock" let a second pipeline in.
  • Cancel is a STATE TRANSITION (Running -> Cancelling), not a UI reset. Idle is reached in
    exactly one place: `FinishAsync`, after the runner's Task has completed.
  • The CancellationTokenSource is created in `StartAsync` and disposed ONLY in
    `FinishAsync`, after the runner's Task has completed. ProcessWorker holds live
    registrations on it until then; disposing earlier is the CANCELREG_01 hang.
  • Shutdown requests cancellation and waits, bounded. A session that outlives the bound stays
    Cancelling — the state never claims Idle on the pipeline's behalf.

Cancel signals the token UNDER the gate, and Finish clears the source under the same gate before
disposing it, so a cancel can never land on a disposed source (no ObjectDisposedException race).
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### ExportCoordinator.Finish — EXPORTSESSION_02 (line 152)

EXPORTSESSION_02 — THE ONE COMPLETION TRANSITION. Runs once per accepted session, strictly
after the runner's Task has completed: Idle, then dispose the source, then notify.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Services/FilmstripPrewarm.cs

### FilmstripPrewarm — PREWARM_01, STRIP_03, THROTTLE_01 (line 10)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
PREWARM_01 — RENDER THE FILM LANE BEFORE ANYONE ASKS FOR IT.

The lane is now fast (STRIP_03: first frame ~0.2s, complete ~0.5s) but it still starts from
nothing at the moment a screen opens. The inputs, however, are known long before that: the
instant the user sets MARK START and MARK END in the Main App, the exact range every filmstrip
will be built from is decided. This renders it then, in the background, so by the time the
Granular editor or the Voice-Over window is opened the strip is usually already sitting in
memory and the lane paints on the first frame.

── ⚠️ THIS IS A PREWARM, NOT A CACHE. READ BEFORE JUDGING IT AGAINST MANDATE #1. ─────────────
Mandate #1 forbids caches "for FFmpeg exports or media generation", and what it is protecting
against is a result OUTLIVING or being REUSED ACROSS jobs — a stale artifact silently standing
in for work that should have been redone. Every property that makes a cache dangerous is
absent here, by construction:
  * SINGLE ENTRY. One strip is held. A new range REPLACES it; there is no store to go stale.
  * MEMORY ONLY. Nothing is written to disk. Nothing survives the process.
  * TAKE-ONCE. `TryTake` removes the strip as it hands it over. It is consumed by
    exactly one screen and can never be served twice, so two windows cannot end up sharing —
    and disposing — one bitmap.
  * INPUT-KEYED AND SELF-INVALIDATING. The key is (path, start, duration, frames). Any change
    to the trim, or a different video, makes the held strip unreachable and cancels the render
    in flight. It cannot answer for a range it was not built from.
  * NOT ON THE EXPORT PATH. This produces a 60px-tall UI decoration. No exported frame, no
    encoder decision and no timing calculation reads it. If it is empty, wrong, or never runs,
    the only consequence is that a lane renders on demand exactly as it does today.
It is the same single render the screen would have started itself, moved earlier in time. If a
future change would make it PERSIST, be REUSED between exports, or feed anything that ends up
in the output file, it stops being this and becomes the thing the mandate forbids.

⚠️ FAILURE IS ALWAYS SILENT AND ALWAYS SAFE. Every caller treats a miss as "render it now".
Do not add throwing, do not add retries, and do not make a screen WAIT on a prewarm — the
whole point is that it is invisible whether it worked or not.

── ⚠️ THROTTLE_01 — THE PREWARM YIELDS TO PLAYBACK, TWO WAYS ──────────────────────────────
A prewarm competes with whatever mpv is doing for the same disk and CPU, and it is the one
strip in the app nobody is waiting for, so it is the ONLY caller that passes a
cooperative-yield gate to `ThumbnailStripGenerator.StreamAsync`:
  * LAYER 1 (never start): while `MpvIpcClient.AnyPlaybackActive` is true, the
    debounce re-queues the job instead of spawning — zero processes, zero disk, one 450ms
    timer retry.
  * LAYER 2 (stop mid-stream): if playback STARTS during a render, the stream reader stops
    consuming; FFmpeg blocks on a full pipe, its I/O drops to zero, and it resumes from the
    cached byte offset the moment playback pauses. The prewarm's OWN token is deliberately
    NOT cancelled by playback: cancelling would throw away every decoded frame and restart
    the process, re-reading from disk the exact blocks already paid for — the opposite of
    the goal. Superseded ranges and app shutdown still cancel instantly, exactly as before.
On-demand strips (a lane a user is watching fill) never pass the gate and never wait.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### FilmstripPrewarm.DebounceMs (line 63)

Debounce before a scheduled render actually starts. Dragging a trim marker fires a change
per pointer move; without this the app would spawn and kill an ffmpeg process per frame of
the drag. Long enough to sit out a drag, short enough that the render is done before the
user can set a trim and open the editor.

### FilmstripPrewarm.MinRangeSec (line 71)

Ranges shorter than this are not worth a process.

### FilmstripPrewarm.Schedule (line 92)

Asks for the strip covering this range to exist by the time somebody wants it. Cheap and
idempotent: re-scheduling the SAME range that is already rendering or already held does
nothing. Call it whenever the trim changes; the debounce absorbs a drag.

### FilmstripPrewarm.TryTake (line 215)

Hands over the pre-rendered strip for this range if there is one, REMOVING it from the
store. Returns null on any mismatch — the caller must always be able to render it itself.

### FilmstripPrewarm.Clear (line 233)

Drops everything. Call when the loaded video changes or the app shuts down.

### GeminiClient — GEMINICLIENT_01 (line 75)

GEMINICLIENT_01 — THE one place the app talks to Google Gemini (docs/05 SYS-AISETTINGS).

- The key travels ONLY in the `x-goog-api-key` header — never in a URL — and every string
that leaves this class for a log, a fault or an exception passes through `Redact`.
- Every attempt has its own timeout (a linked token). A timeout is reported as
`GeminiErrorKind.Timeout`, never as the user's own cancel: before this class the 60 s
`HttpClient.Timeout` surfaced as `OperationCanceledException` and the editor told
the user they had cancelled.
- Transient failures retry with back-off, honouring Google's `RetryInfo.retryDelay` /
`Retry-After`. A DAILY quota is not retried (it will not clear in seconds).
- Errors are classified from Google's JSON error body (`API_KEY_INVALID` arrives as HTTP 400,
not 401) into a sentence the user can act on.

The Magic Wand's `GeminiHudDetectionService` shares the constants, redaction, model
resolution and response parsing below, but keeps its own no-retry transport by design (TL-AIHUD).

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Services/GeminiHudDetectionService.cs

### GeminiHudDetectionService — AIHUD_01, AIPROVIDER_ROUTING_01 (line 19)

AIHUD_01 — Google Gemini as an OPTIONAL Magic Wand assistant.

**What it sends.** ONE still: the frozen frame, as a JPEG, plus a text prompt. Never
the video, never a clip, never a path. The prompt asks only for persistent gameplay HUD and
explicitly excludes people, enemies, world objects, held weapons and scenery.

**What it returns.** An `AiHudDetectionResult` whose candidates have passed
`AiHudResponseParser` — normalized 0..1 source-frame boxes. It does not convert to
pixels (that happens exactly once, in `HudDetectionCoordinator`), it does not fuse,
and it holds no UI types.

**Credentials.** The key travels ONLY in the `x-goog-api-key` request header —
never in the URL, so no URL this class builds, logs or reports is secret-bearing. Every string
that leaves this class (log line, fault detail, result detail) is passed through
`Redact` first. The key is read from the provider at call time and never stored,
cached or serialized.

**Failure.** Never throws for provider trouble — see `IAiHudDetectionService`.
No retry: a Magic Wand user is waiting, and the local answer is already on its way, so a 429 or
a timeout falls straight back rather than holding the button.

AIPROVIDER_ROUTING_01 — routes requests through selected IAiVisionProvider.

### GeminiHudDetectionService.DefaultModel (line 45)

D3 — one default model for the whole app: `GeminiClient.DefaultModel`.

### GeminiHudDetectionService.SharedClient (line 54)

One process-wide client for production (socket reuse). Per-request timeouts are
enforced with a linked token, so the client's own timeout is infinite.

### GeminiHudDetectionService.GeminiHudDetectionService (line 78)

**apiKeyProvider:** Read at call time; the key is never retained.
**modelProvider:** Read at call time; an unsafe or empty name falls back to `DefaultModel`.
**faults:** Where caught failures go (Recoverable — the coordinator owns the user-facing tier).
**httpClient:** Test seam. Null uses the shared production client.
**timeout:** Per-request ceiling. Null uses `DefaultTimeout`.
**log:** Test seam for log capture. Null writes to `CoreLogger`.
**cache:** Null creates a private bounded cache.
**vendorProvider:** Optional delegate returning the active AiVendor for U3 HUD detection.
**visionProvider:** Optional vision provider override for tests or custom dispatch.

The model name that will actually be used: the configured one if it is a plain
identifier, otherwise `DefaultModel`. Never lets text into the URL path that
could change its meaning.

### GeminiHudDetectionService.Fail (line 214)

Logs (redacted) and returns a non-success result. Caught exceptions are reported at the
catch site as Recoverable — WITHOUT the raw exception object, whose message and stack are
not ours to vouch for — and the coordinator raises the one user-facing Degraded notice with
the local results already in hand.

### GeminiHudDetectionService.Redact (line 227)

Removes the key (and anything shaped like a `key=` query value) from text bound for a

### ExportState — EXPORTSESSION_02 (line 7)

EXPORTSESSION_02 — the three states an export session can be in. There is no fourth.

`Running -> Cancelling -> Idle`. Cancelling is NOT Idle: the token has been signalled but the
pipeline (FFmpeg kill grace, reader-pipe drain, job temp directory delete) has not finished
unwinding. Nothing may re-arm PROCESS until the coordinator itself reports Idle.

### ExportOutcome — EXPORTSESSION_02 (line 23)

EXPORTSESSION_02 — how one export session ended.

### ExportOutcome.Succeeded (line 26)

The render finished and was delivered.

### ExportOutcome.Failed (line 29)

The render failed, or the runner threw (see `ExportCompletion.Error`).

### ExportOutcome.Cancelled (line 32)

The user (or shutdown) cancelled, and the pipeline has stopped.

### ExportOutcome.Declined (line 35)

Pre-flight did not start a render: nothing loaded, no output folder chosen, or the user backed
out of the high-segment-count prompt. The runner has already told the user why.

### ExportOutcome.Rejected (line 41)

The single-flight gate refused this request because another session was Running or
Cancelling. No state transition happened and no completion notification fired.

### IExportRunner — EXPORTSESSION_02 (line 48)

EXPORTSESSION_02 — the work an export session performs. The coordinator owns WHEN it runs and
for how long its token lives; the runner owns WHAT it does (payload, FFmpeg graph, encoder
policy, dialogs). The token is valid — never disposed — until the returned Task has completed.

### DelegateExportRunner (line 58)

Adapts a delegate to `IExportRunner` (the Main App's PROCESS pipeline).

### ExportRequest — EXPORTSESSION_02 (line 69)

EXPORTSESSION_02 — one immutable request to export. Created by the window, consumed once.
**Origin:** Who asked (for the log), e.g. "PROCESS button".
**Runner:** The pipeline to run under the coordinator's token.

### ExportCompletion — EXPORTSESSION_02 (line 74)

EXPORTSESSION_02 — the final result of one session, delivered exactly once.
**Outcome:** How it ended.
**Error:**
The exception the runner threw, if any. An `OperationCanceledException` here means
the runner was cancelled by throwing; any other type means it failed by throwing and the caller
MUST surface it (the coordinator never swallows it).

**CancelRequested:** True when `IExportCoordinator.Cancel` reached this session.

### IExportCoordinator — EXPORTSESSION_02 (line 84)

EXPORTSESSION_02 — EXPORT LIFECYCLE OWNER (03 §8b FFM-EXPORTLIFETIME).

Owns the Idle/Running/Cancelling state, the `CancellationTokenSource`, the in-flight
Task, the single-flight gate, Cancel, the final result and the exactly-once completion
transition. Does NOT own FFmpeg graph construction, encoder policy, ProcessWorker or any control.

### IExportCoordinator.State (line 95)

Current state. Thread-safe snapshot.

### IExportCoordinator.StateChanged (line 98)

Raised on every state transition, on the thread that caused it.

### IExportCoordinator.Completed (line 101)

Raised exactly once per accepted session, after the Idle transition.

### IExportCoordinator.StartAsync (line 104)

Starts a session if Idle; otherwise returns `ExportOutcome.Rejected` immediately
without touching the running session. The returned Task completes after the session is Idle
and its token source disposed. It never faults: a runner exception is returned in
`ExportCompletion.Error`.

### IExportCoordinator.Cancel (line 112)

Running -> Cancelling: signals the token. Does NOT transition to Idle; that happens only when
the runner's Task completes. Returns true only for the call that performed the transition.

### IExportCoordinator.ShutdownAsync (line 118)

Shutdown: requests cancellation and waits — bounded by `timeout` — for the
session to reach Idle. Returns true when nothing is running on return.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Services/InProcessSessionState.cs

### InProcessSessionState — UISTATE_01, IPCDEADLINE_01, UIIPC_01 (line 7)

UISTATE_01 — THE TYPED READ-ONLY SNAPSHOT SERVICE FOR UI CONSTRUCTION (Architectural Fix #3).

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
WHAT THIS REPLACES. Window construction used to call `StateTransferStore.LoadSync()`, which
can: inspect/start the named-pipe server (including `TryStart`'s 1-second ready wait),
create directories, connect to the pipe as a client, and acquire a NAMED SYSTEM MUTEX with a
default timeout of 15 SECONDS — all on the Avalonia UI thread, in a constructor. Every window
that called `WindowBoundsHelper.Track` paid that price before it appeared.

THE CONTRACT HERE IS THE OPPOSITE, IN ORDER:

- **In-process live state.** `BootstrapAsync` (Program.cs) runs BEFORE any window
exists and loads the session state asynchronously, which starts the in-process
`NamedPipeStateServer` holding it in memory. When that server is running,
`ReadSnapshot` is a lock + deep clone — pure memory, no pipe, no mutex, no I/O.
- **Real cross-process case.** No in-process server means this is a standalone tool
process next to a running main app. Bootstrap has already loaded that LIVE state asynchronously
(bounded pipe exchange, IPCDEADLINE_01) and primed `SessionStateWriter` with it, so
this is still a memory read.
- **Never blocks.** UIIPC_01: no pipe, no mutex, no disk on this path. If nothing was primed
yet the result is the not-yet-acknowledged updates alone, and an asynchronous prime is started
for the next read. (This used to fall back to `NamedPipeStateClient.GetStateSync`, whose
`ReadFrame` had no deadline: a peer that connected and never answered froze the window.)

This is a read path only. Writes (bounds, preferences) go through `SessionStateWriter.Enqueue`,
whose pending values are overlaid on every snapshot, so a read always sees the latest write.

### InProcessSessionState.ReadSnapshot — UISTATE_01, UIIPC_01 (line 40)

UISTATE_01 — a read-only snapshot of the session state, safe to call from UI construction.
Never starts a server, never waits on the IPC ready event, never takes the named mutex, never
touches the pipe or the disk (UIIPC_01).

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Services/LegacyRecoveryMigrator.cs

### LegacyRecoveryMigrator — RECOVERYDOC_08, PROJ_02, AOTSAFETY_01 (line 9)

RECOVERYDOC_08 - ONE-WAY legacy recovery migration: old recovery_v2 payload - canonical
`ProjectDocument`.

WHY A READER AND NOT A WRITER: users arriving from a crash written by an older build have a
legacy `schemaVersion:1` payload on disk. It is parsed ONCE, reconstructed into a real
document, applied through the normal restore path, and the very next autosave overwrites the
file in the canonical envelope format. The legacy shape is never written again - maintaining
two writers is precisely the defect this mission removes.

DOCUMENTED LIMITATIONS (the legacy schema genuinely never carried these): Mask (the legacy
payload recorded HUD toggle positions but not the mask snapshot, so a migrated session falls
back to whatever mask is machine-active now, exactly as the old restore did); Merge/EDL (the
merger queue lived in the merger window and was never in the legacy payload); and the source
fingerprint (size/mtime/fps/width/height were never recorded - the migrated document records
the path and the measured duration only, so source-integrity checks report Unknown instead of
nagging). Everything the legacy payload DID carry - trims, base speed, speed segments with
zoom boxes, cuts, meme placements, music bed and voice-over placement, export quality and
portrait mode - is reconstructed faithfully.

NO REFLECTION: JsonNode only (PROJ_02 / AOTSAFETY_01).

### LegacyRecoveryMigrator.TryMigrate (line 36)

Converts a legacy payload. Returns a document plus the crash-only transient metadata that
sat beside the project fields in the old file. False with `error` set
means the payload carried no project worth restoring.

### LegacyRecoveryMigrator.ReadCuts (line 133)

Legacy cuts are ABSOLUTE source milliseconds; the document stores CLIP-RELATIVE seconds
(OutputTimeline.Cut) - the same conversion ProjectSession.Capture performs.

### LegacyRecoveryMigrator.LegacyTransientKeys (line 192)

is reconstructed into the ProjectDocument instead - this list is the inventory of what
stayed transient, never a second project schema.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Services/LegacyScheduledTask.cs

### LegacyScheduledTask — NOHIDDENTOOLS_01, NOSYSTEMTASK_01 (line 5)

NOHIDDENTOOLS_01 — answers "does a scheduled task of this name exist?" WITHOUT starting a program.

Releases before NOSYSTEMTASK_01 created a scheduled task. Cleaning it up used to start the hidden
Windows task tool on every install, uninstall and maintenance run, on every PC, although almost no
PC still has the task. A program that keeps starting hidden system tools is what antivirus
behaviour rules score (SYS-AVCLEAN). The tool now runs only when this says the task is there.

Two read-only checks, either is enough: the task's definition file in the Windows task folder
(readable by administrators) and the task's entry in the Task Scheduler's registry index
(readable by every user). Any doubt answers false: nothing is deleted on a guess.

Spec: docs/05_SYSTEM_LIFECYCLE_STORAGE.md #SYS-AVCLEAN.

### LegacyScheduledTask.IsPlainName (line 44)

A task in the root folder: a single name, no path separators (pure, unit-tested).

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Services/ProjectRecoveryService.cs

### ProjectRecoveryService — RECOVERYDOC_04, WRITEORDER_01 (line 10)

RECOVERYDOC_04 — THE RECOVERY BRIDGE, NOT A SECOND PROJECT SCHEMA.

This service used to OWN a parallel, hand-maintained 60-field JSON model of the user's project
(`SerializeState` + a matching field-by-field restore). Every project feature therefore
needed two serialisations, and every one that was forgotten was silently lost on crash
recovery. That schema is GONE.

The recovery file now holds exactly one `ProjectDocument` — captured from
ProjectSession.Capture, serialised by the canonical `ProjectSerializer` inside
`RecoveryEnvelope` — plus crash-only transient metadata (see
`RecoveryEnvelope.Write` for what qualifies). Disk writes still go through
`RecoveryManager`, which keeps the atomic write protocol (05 §4 SYS-ATOMICWRITE)
and the WRITEORDER_01 save/clear ordering, and still preserves an active
`granular_session` sub-object across app-level saves (SYS-RECOVERY).

ARCHITECTURE GUARD: do not reintroduce project fields here or in the envelope. If a project
property is missing from recovery, it is missing from `ProjectDocument` — fix it
THERE, once, and both normal saves and recovery gain it.

### ProjectRecoveryService.SaveState — RECOVERYDOC_06, EDITHOT_02 (line 45)

RECOVERYDOC_06 — the ONLY recovery write. Persists the canonical document captured from the
live session inside the `RecoveryEnvelope`. Atomic, ordered, debounced by the
caller (EDITHOT_02) — none of that changed.

### ProjectRecoveryService.LoadSnapshot — RECOVERYDOC_07 (line 59)

RECOVERYDOC_07 — loads the recovery snapshot. Legacy schemaVersion-1 payloads (written
before the canonical envelope) are returned with `RecoverySnapshot.IsLegacy` set
and `RecoverySnapshot.LegacyRaw` populated; `LegacyRecoveryMigrator`
converts them once and the next autosave writes the canonical format. Nothing here WRITES
the legacy format — there is one writer, and it is the envelope.

### ProjectRecoveryService.HasUnsavedWork — SWITCHPROMPT_01 (line 89)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
"Is there anything here a user would be upset to lose?"

Two consumers, and they pull in the same direction: it decides whether a recovery snapshot
is worth writing, and (SWITCHPROMPT_01) whether the Video Merger / Crop Tools hand-off is
worth interrupting with a confirmation.

⚠️ A LOADED VIDEO IS NOT WORK. Uploading a clip and touching nothing else must return false.

SWITCHPROMPT_01 — TWO REASONS THIS RETURNED TRUE ON A COMPLETELY EMPTY EDITOR, which is why
the switch prompt fired with nothing loaded:

  1. The toggle comparisons were against HARDCODED assumptions — portrait on, fade on,
     speed 1.1 — rather than against the defaults the user actually configured in
     Settings → Defaults. Anyone who set "Portrait Mode: off", or a default speed of 1.0,
     had a session that was born dirty: the very first frame after startup already
     disagreed with the constants below, with no video and no edit in sight. Every one of
     those comparisons now reads the SAME defaults ApplyDefaults() seeds the session from,
     so "unchanged from where the app put it" reliably means unchanged.

  2. Nothing checked whether a video was loaded at all. With no clip there is no project:
     no trim to keep, nothing to recover, nothing to warn about. That is now the first
     question asked, and it is the guard that makes the empty-editor case impossible
     regardless of what any toggle says.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Unchanged in behaviour: this is a LIVE-SESSION predicate (docs/06 §8 — the close-path
guard, SWITCHPROMPT_01), never a recovery-JSON reader. It answers "does the CURRENT editor
differ from its defaults"; the persisted document's emptiness backstop is
`RecoveryEnvelope.HasContent`.

### RecoverySnapshot — RECOVERYDOC_07 (line 151)

RECOVERYDOC_07 — one loaded recovery snapshot. Exactly one of the two shapes is present: a
canonical envelope (`Document` + `TransientMetadata`) or a legacy
pre-envelope payload (`LegacyRaw`, converted once by
`LegacyRecoveryMigrator`). `Raw` is the untouched file root — kept only
for crash-only sub-objects that live beside the envelope (the granular editor's
`granular_session`, merged there by RecoveryManager per SYS-RECOVERY). It is NEVER a
second project model.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Services/ProjectSession.cs

### ProjectSession — PROJSESSION_01, PROJSESSION_02, AUTOSAVEBG_01 (line 15)

PROJSESSION_01 — THE DOCUMENT THE USER IS EDITING, AND ITS HISTORY.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
WHY THIS EXISTS — TWO DEFECTS, ONE CAUSE.

**1. The application could not save.** `ProjectDocument`, `ProjectSerializer`, `ProjectStore`
and `RecentProjects` were fully written, specified (06), and covered by ~370 lines of test —
and a grep for any of them across `src/FreeVideoStudio.App/` returned **nothing**.
There was no Save, no Open, no recent list and no autosave. A user who spent forty minutes on
speed ramps, memes and a music bed and closed the window lost all of it, with no prompt.

**2. Undo was three private implementations and one dead one.** `Core/Undo/UndoStack<T>`
was specified by 07 and tested, and never instantiated. `GranularSpeedEditorWindow` kept its own
`List`-based `_undoStack`/`_redoStack`; `CropToolWindow` had a third; and **`MainWindow` had no
undo at all** — no Ctrl+Z on the main timeline, where trims, cuts, memes and the music bed are
decided.

Both are the same cause: **there was no object that WAS the user's work.** State lived in
whichever window happened to own the control that produced it. This class is that object.
Everything else follows from it — you can save a document, you can keep a stack of documents,
and you can hand one to another window without serialising it through a named pipe.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

**PROJSESSION_02 — capture is a PROJECTION, not a second source of truth.** The view-models
remain where the live editing state lives; this class reads them to build a document and writes
a document back into them. It deliberately does NOT hold a parallel copy that could drift.
`Capture()` is cheap and is called at edit boundaries, not per frame.

**THREADING.** UI thread only. It reads and writes view-model properties bound to controls.
The one exception is `AutosaveTick`: it is invoked from a dispatcher timer and
captures its snapshot on the UI thread, but (AUTOSAVEBG_01) the atomic write, the hardware
flush and the history sidecar run on the thread pool, and only the dirty-flag update is
marshalled back. Explicit saves await the same ordered background I/O queue.

PROJSESSION_03 — autosave cadence. The RecoveryManager already snapshots continuously for
crash recovery (05 §4); this is different — it keeps the user's NAMED file current so a
power cut does not cost the last hour. Only fires when dirty AND a path is known.

AUTOSAVEBG_01 — WRITE-BEHIND. The UI thread does only the in-memory work: capture the

⚠️ ONE WRITE IN FLIGHT. A tick that finds the previous write unfinished skips; the next

their edit omitted the single setting that decides what the frame looks like.

document that never existed on this timeline, silently.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Services/ProtectedWorkerStage.cs

### ProtectedWorkerStage — WORKERSTAGE_01 (line 9)

WORKERSTAGE_01 — THE ELEVATED UPDATE WORKER RUNS ONLY FROM A FOLDER ITS OWN USER CANNOT CHANGE
(05 SYS-UPGRADE-TRUST).

⚠️ WHY. The worker — the only part of an install or update that runs as administrator — used
to be copied into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\FreeVideoStudioUpdates\Stage\<id>` and started from there
with `Verb = "runas"`. Every program the user runs can write to that folder. Between the copy
and the user's "Yes" on the Windows prompt, anything running as the user could swap the file or drop
a DLL beside it, and the user — who EXPECTS a prompt at that moment, and whose prompt says "Unknown
publisher" for this certificate anyway — would hand it administrator rights.

The copy now lives in `%ProgramData%\FreeVideoStudio-Worker-<random>\FreeVideoStudio.exe`:

- The folder is created with a PROTECTED access list (nothing inherited): SYSTEM and
  Administrators full control; the user read/execute only. The `OWNER RIGHTS` entry takes away the
  rights an owner normally keeps implicitly (changing the access list), and gives the creator ONLY
  "add a file". Standard users have no "delete child" right on `%ProgramData%` itself, so the folder
  cannot be renamed or replaced either.
- The program file is created WITH its final access list (read/execute for the user) by this
  process, which keeps the one write handle it was granted at creation; nobody else can ever open it
  for writing, delete it or rename it.
- The protection is PROVEN, not assumed: after the file is written, writing, deleting and
  renaming are attempted and must all be refused; the folder must hold exactly that one file; the
  copy must hash to the bytes that were written and (Release builds) carry the publisher's
  signature. Any doubt stops the update before Windows is asked — there is no fallback to the
  user-writable folder.
- A read handle that denies writers is held until the elevated process has started.
- The worker refuses to run elevated from anywhere else (`IsProtectedWorkerPath`,
  checked in `UpgradeInstallWorker.RunAsync`) and restricts its own DLL search to System32
  (`NativeHelpers.RestrictDllSearchToSystem32`), so a file added to the folder is never loaded.

The user cannot delete these folders; the elevated worker removes old ones at the end of every
install (`SweepStale`, from `MaintainAsync`) and the uninstaller removes them all.

### ProtectedWorkerStage.FolderPath (line 57)

The protected folder.

### ProtectedWorkerStage.ExecutablePath (line 60)

The verified worker copy to start with `Verb = "runas"`.

### ProtectedWorkerStage.Root (line 63)

`%ProgramData%`: the only per-machine folder a standard user may create in but not rename in.

### ProtectedWorkerStage.Create (line 66)

Copies `sourceExecutable` into a new protected folder and proves the protection.
Throws `IOException` (plain English) when Windows does not allow it.

### ProtectedWorkerStage.IsProtectedWorkerPath (line 122)

True only for `%ProgramData%\FreeVideoStudio-Worker-<32 hex>\FreeVideoStudio.exe`.
The worker checks its own path with this before doing anything as administrator.

### ProtectedWorkerStage.ExistingFolders (line 149)

Every worker folder that exists (for the elevated sweep and the uninstaller).

### ProtectedWorkerStage.SweepStale (line 166)

Elevated only. Removes every worker folder except the one this process runs from. A folder still
in use is left for the next install. Returns how many were removed.

### ProtectedWorkerStage.Dispose (line 190)

Releases the deny-writers handle. Call right after the elevated process has started.

### ProtectedWorkerStage.OwnerRights (line 200)

S-1-3-4: replaces the owner's implicit READ_CONTROL/WRITE_DAC with exactly what it grants.

### ProtectedWorkerStage.ProveLocked (line 228)

Each of these must be REFUSED. One that succeeds means the folder is not protected.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Services/ShellLauncher.cs

### ShellLauncher — SHELLLAUNCH_01 (line 8)

SHELLLAUNCH_01 — the one place the app hands something to Windows to open (a web page, a
folder, a file in its default app, an elevated helper).

`Process.Start(ProcessStartInfo)` returns a `Process` that wraps a native
process HANDLE. Twenty call sites threw that object away, so each launch leaked a handle until
the garbage collector happened to finalise it — and finalisers are the last thing a NativeAOT
app should lean on. Every launch now disposes the wrapper immediately: the launched program is
unaffected (disposing the wrapper never stops the process), only our handle is released.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Services/StartupCrashGuard.cs

### StartupCrashGuard — CRASHLOOP_01, RETAIN_02, ISSUE_02 (line 6)

CRASHLOOP_01 — WHAT HAPPENS WHEN AN UPDATE THAT PASSED ITS CHECKS STILL WILL NOT START.

The first-launch health check (05 SYS-UPGRADE) proves the new version starts once; after the
commit the previous version's files are only a backup. A build that then crashes on every start left
the user with nothing but "reinstall by hand" — and no hint where to find the previous installer.

Every main-window start counts an attempt for the running version; a window that stays open for
`StableAfter` resets the count. From the `OfferAfter`th failed start in a row,
the user is told plainly and offered the release page, which keeps the installers of the last five
versions (RETAIN_02); an older installer asks before going back (ISSUE_02). The app then starts as
usual. Nothing is uninstalled or downloaded by itself; it costs nothing.

### StartupCrashGuard.OfferAfter (line 23)

Failed starts in a row (of the same version) before the user is offered the way back.

### StartupCrashGuard.StableAfter (line 26)

How long the main window must stay open for a start to count as good.
