### near AppZoomAntsColor — ZOOMANTS_01 (line 35)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ZOOMANTS_01 — THE MARCHING-ANTS YELLOW, AND WHY IT IS A DELIBERATE EXCEPTION.
⚠️ READ IDEA_6 DIRECTLY ABOVE BEFORE TOUCHING THIS. IDEA_6 says everything zoom wears
AppZoomColor and zoom must not be given "a second colour for contrast" — and it names
yellow #fde047 as one of the three colours that were REMOVED from zoom precisely
because users could not tell a zoom from a speed segment.
This token reintroduces that yellow for ONE thing only: the animated 1px marching-ants
outline of the zoom rubber-band, on the owner's explicit instruction. The reasoning is
that an ANIMATED hairline is distinguished by its motion rather than by its hue, so it
no longer relies on colour to be told apart from a static speed block.

AppWarningBrush (#facc15) and to the selected-block highlight. If zoom and "selected"

revert — set it to {StaticResource AppZoomColor} and the ants go back to zoom blue.

### near AppScrimSoftBrush — SCRIM_01 (line 80)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SCRIM_01 — THE THREE DIM LAYERS, AS TOKENS.

Six windows each carried their own black-with-alpha literal for "dim what is behind
this": #E6000000 four times (MemeSwapOverlay in Main, Granular, Music Wizard and
Voice Over), #F0000000 once (MemeRebuildOverlay) and #90000000 once (the Merger's
FlyoutScrim). Nothing enforced that the four identical ones stayed identical, and
Invariant #5 forbids the literal outright.

Deliberately theme-INVARIANT, exactly like AppOverlayBrush above: a scrim's job is to
push the content behind it away from the eye, and on a light ground a light scrim does
not do that. Black at three strengths, in both ThemeVariants.

Pick by intent, not by number:
Soft   — a flyout is open; the page behind is still legible context.
(base) — a blocking operation owns the window; the page behind is unavailable.
Strong — a rebuild is discarding and re-laying-out what is behind it.

### near Height — SLIDER_04 (line 1129)

⚠️ SLIDER_04 — WIDTH IS 52, NOT 44, AND THAT NUMBER IS DERIVED, NOT TASTE.
The knob is a 26px Ellipse that grows to scale(2.0) while held = 52px rendered.
`Track` centres the thumb in its reserved slot, so the dot's centre can never get
closer to either end than HALF the thumb's width. At 44 that is 22px, and a 52px
dot centred 22px in reaches 4px PAST the slider's own left edge — which is why the
knob appeared sliced at 0% and 100%: it was painting outside its parent and being
covered by whatever sat beside it.
52 = the largest rendered dot, so at the extremes the dot lands exactly flush with
the slider edge and never leaves its own bounds. If you ever change the press
scale or the 26px Ellipse, RECOMPUTE THIS (and the rail inset below, which must
stay at half this value). Height stays 44: the vertical overflow is handled by
margins on the hosting rows, not by the thumb.

### near Template (line 1145)

THE KNOB MUST BE A DOT — and this is the ONLY reliable way to guarantee it.
Forcing the thumb to 44x44 above made it render as a SQUARE, because Fluent's stock
Thumb template does not honour CornerRadius: setting CornerRadius on the Thumb had
no effect at all (verified on a real run). Rather than keep guessing at the theme's
internals, the template is replaced outright with a single Ellipse.
The Ellipse has no Width/Height so it stretches to whatever size the Width/Height
setters above give the thumb, which keeps the 44px hit target intact, and it is
filled from the thumb's own Background so every hover/pressed Background override
below still works untouched. Avalonia's default RenderTransformOrigin is the
centre, so scale(1.3) on hover and scale(2.0) while held grow the dot from its
middle and spring back through the existing 0.3s transform transition.

### near Ellipse (line 1158)

The Panel keeps the FULL 44x44 hit target (Background must stay non-null or
it stops hit-testing), while the visible dot is a fixed 21px centred inside
it. Letting the Ellipse stretch made the knob 44px wide — correct as a
touch target, far too fat as a knob. Hit area and visible size are two
different things here and must stay separate.
RenderTransform scale on the thumb scales this child with it, so the
hover/press growth below still works off the 21px base.

### near AppInfoBrush (line 1172)

Explicit resting fill. The template above draws the dot from the thumb's OWN
Background, so it must not be left to whatever Fluent happened to set: if the stock
theme painted its fill on an inner element rather than on Background, the dot would
come out invisible — worse than the square it replaces. Pinning it here also gives
the BrushTransition below a real value to animate FROM into the hover glow.
This is the resting knob colour; change this one token to restyle it.

### near PART_DecreaseButton — SLIDER_01, SLIDER_04 (line 1198)

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SLIDER_01 — THE BROKEN TRACK LINE.

`Track` lays out DecreaseButton | Thumb | IncreaseButton and reserves the thumb's
LAYOUT width for the middle slot. That width is 44px (the suite's grab target), while
the visible knob is a 26px Ellipse — and RenderTransform scaling does NOT change
layout width, so the reserved gap stays 44px at every size.

Measured result: 44px gap around a 26px dot leaves NINE PIXELS OF BARE TRACK ON EACH
SIDE at rest. The rail reads as two separate horizontal lines with the knob floating
between them, which is exactly what it looks like on screen. (At scale(2.0) the dot
grows to 52px and finally covers the gap — so the break appears to heal while
dragging and returns on release, which makes it read as a glitch rather than a style.)

FIX PART 1 — CLOSE THE GAP: pull each half of the rail 22px INTO the thumb's slot with
a negative margin, so the two halves meet underneath the knob and the line is
continuous at every size. 26 = half the 52px thumb (SLIDER_04). These two numbers MUST stay in step.

FIX PART 2 — THE RAIL MUST ALSO END WHERE THE DOT ENDS: because Track reserves the
thumb's 44px, the thumb CENTRE can only travel from 22px to (width - 22px). A rail
drawn the full width therefore has 22px at each end the dot can never reach — at 100%
you see bare rail to the RIGHT of the dot, at 0% to its LEFT. So each half ALSO gets a
POSITIVE margin on its OUTER edge, insetting the rail to exactly [22, width-22], which
is precisely the dot's travel range. Dot and rail now start and finish together.
Decrease: left  +22 (inset)   right -22 (meet under the thumb)
Increase: left  -22 (meet)    right +22 (inset)

⚠️ NAME-TARGETED, SO IT FAILS SAFE. If a future Avalonia theme renames these template
parts the selectors simply match nothing and the rail goes back to being split — ugly,
never broken. Do NOT "fix" this by shrinking the Thumb to 26px: that would drop the
grab target from 44px to 26px and break the Font-Scale/hit-target rule in Section 4.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### near scale (line 1253)

================================================================================
KNOB HOVER / PRESS — the selectors target the THUMB's own pseudo-classes, not the
slider's. This is deliberate and fixes two real faults:

STUTTER: `Slider:pointerover` fires for the whole 44px-tall track row. On every
timeline the seek Canvas (TimelineMarkersCanvas et al) sits ON TOP of the slider and
is hit-testable, so dragging the mouse across the timeline handed hover back and forth
between the two — the knob grew and shrank repeatedly, which read as a flicker.
`Thumb:pointerover` only fires over the knob itself, so crossing the track cannot
retrigger it. It also matches the intended behaviour: the glow belongs to the dot.

NO GROWTH WHILE DRAGGING: `Slider:pressed` is not raised while the THUMB is being
dragged — the thumb captures the pointer, so the slider never enters its pressed state
and the knob stayed small for the whole drag. `Thumb:pressed` is set by the thumb for
exactly as long as the button is held, which is the "grows and stays large until
released" behaviour. The slider-level selector is kept underneath as a harmless
fallback for clicks that land on the track rather than the knob.

ORDER MATTERS: :pressed must come after :pointerover, or the hover scale would win
while dragging (the pointer is also over the thumb).
================================================================================

### near knobhover (line 1286)

================================================================================
TIMELINE KNOB — driven by CLASSES, not pseudo-classes. See Controls/TimelineKnob.cs.
On every timeline the seek Canvas covers the Slider and takes all pointer input, so
the Thumb never gets :pointerover or :pressed and the Slider only gets :pointerover
intermittently (in the thin band where it peeks past the canvas — that intermittency
WAS the flicker). TimelineKnob.Attach flips these two classes from the canvas instead,
which is the surface the user actually touches.
knobdrag comes last so a held drag always beats hover.
================================================================================

### near PART_DecreaseButton — SLIDER_07 (line 1315)

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SLIDER_07 — WHY A VERTICAL SLIDER CANNOT BE NARROWED BY SETTING ITS WIDTH.

An earlier `MixFader` class trimmed the Thumb's Width to 30 and gave the Slider
Width="30". It rendered WRONG: the rail hugged the tray's right edge and the knob was
sliced clean in half down its middle.

THE REASON IS THE STOCK TEMPLATE'S COLUMN LAYOUT. Fluent's vertical Slider is a Grid
whose TRACK column is `Auto` and whose neighbouring tick-bar column is `*`. The star
column absorbs EVERY pixel of width beyond the track's natural size, so the track does
NOT centre — it is pushed hard against one edge, and the Thumb, which centres on the
TRACK, ends up centred on that edge with half its dot outside the Slider's own bounds.
Whatever sits beside it then covers that half.

So the width of a vertical slider is not a free parameter: it IS the thumb's width.
Giving the control any more buys dead space on one side and a clipped knob, not a
wider grab area — and giving it less clips the knob outright. The only honest lever is
the THUMB, and the suite already has one: `CompactSlider` below, whose own note names
"vertical volume" as its case.

⚠️ DO NOT set Width or MinWidth on a vertical Slider to make it narrower, and do not
re-add a thumb-width override without first replacing the template's column layout so
the track actually centres.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
UX AUDIT — ISSUE_10, ISSUE_16, ISSUE_23, ISSUE_30, ISSUE_02, ISSUE_03.

### near AppFontFamily — ISSUE_30 (line 1643)

ISSUE_30: a single font family token with a real fallback chain, and a line-height
floor. Previously the whole 1200-line dictionary declared neither: the app loaded one
family with no backup, so any glyph it did not cover fell back to whatever the OS
picked, and vertical rhythm was left entirely to Fluent's defaults.

### near FixedLineHeight — TEXTCLIP_01, ISSUE_30 (line 1650)

⚠️ TEXTCLIP_01 — DO NOT PUT `LineHeight` BACK ON A BARE `TextBlock` SELECTOR. ⚠️
ISSUE_30 wanted a line-height FLOOR. Avalonia's LineHeight is NOT a floor: when it is
set, TextLineMetrics uses it as the line box height OUTRIGHT, and the baseline is
positioned from it rather than from the font. So a single hard 18px applied to EVERY
TextBlock in the app clipped text at BOTH ends of the size range:
- Anything above ~14px (every AppFontSize16/18/20/24/28/36/48/60 heading, icon and
hero glyph) has a natural line box TALLER than 18px, so its descenders and the
bottoms of round caps were cut off. That is why every Settings section title and
the "Drag & drop your gameplay video here" hero line rendered clipped.
- The 18px box also never scaled: AppLineHeightNormal is NOT in ThemeManager's
s_scaledTokens, so raising Settings > Appearance > Font Size grew every glyph
while the line box stayed frozen at 18px, making the clipping worse at every step.
Removing the setter restores the font's own metrics, which are correct by construction
at every size and every font scale. The token below is kept as an OPT-IN class for the
few places that genuinely want a fixed rhythm — apply `Classes="FixedLineHeight"`
there, never app-wide.

### near Transparent — ISSUE_02 (line 1670)

ISSUE_02: the timeline scrub surfaces carried Background="Transparent" as a LOCAL
attribute, and in Avalonia a locally-set value outranks any style setter - so the
hover and focus tints defined for Canvas.TimelineSeekSurface / Grid.TimelineSeekSurface
could never paint. The resting transparent fill is set HERE instead (it must exist,
or the Canvas stops hit-testing and seeking breaks), and the local attributes are
removed from every consumer so the state styles finally win.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Controls/PhoneFrameMockup.axaml

### near ColumnDefinitions (line 5)

================================================================================================
PORTRAIT PREVIEW GUIDE — COORDINATE SPACE IS *SOURCE* PIXELS (1920x1080), NOT OUTPUT PIXELS.
================================================================================================
This control is an OVERLAY drawn on top of the live 16:9 video, so its unit space is the SOURCE
frame. The centre column (720 units) is the "portrait brick wall": the slice of the source that
survives the Portrait Canvas Trick (1280 internal width / (16/9) = 720 source px).

⚠️ THE BUG THAT WAS FIXED HERE — READ BEFORE CHANGING ANY NUMBER BELOW ⚠️
The phone SCREEN used to be 720x1080 with 150-unit black bars drawn INSIDE it. Both numbers
were wrong, because 150 is a measurement in the 1080x1920 OUTPUT space and this grid is in
1080-tall SOURCE space. The consequences were:
* the "phone" was 720x1080 = 2:3, which is the aspect of the VIDEO CONTENT AREA, not of a
phone screen (a phone is 9:16);
* the bars painted solid black over source rows 0-150 and 930-1080 — 300 of the 1080
surviving rows, i.e. 27.8% of the picture — which are FULLY VISIBLE in the exported file.
That made the preview contradict both the export and the zoom rubberband: the rubberband
correctly let the user draw into those rows (they really are exported), while this overlay
insisted they were dead space. Verified against the real filter chain
(scale=3414:1920,crop=1280:1920:1066:0,scale=1080:1620,pad=1080:1920:0:150): source row Y maps
to output row 150 + Y*1.5, so source 0..1080 -> output 150..1770. NOTHING in the source is ever
hidden by the bars; they are pure added canvas.

CORRECT GEOMETRY (all in source units, 720 = the surviving slice width):
output px -> source units  =  720 / 1080  =  2/3
screen height  1920 output px * 2/3 = 1280 units   (720x1280 = 9:16 ✓)
bar height      150 output px * 2/3 =  100 units   (x2 = 200)
video area                          = 1080 units   (100 + 1080 + 100 = 1280 ✓)
The 1080-unit video band therefore aligns EXACTLY with the live video underneath, and the bars
sit OUTSIDE it — which is why the screen deliberately overflows the 1080-tall grid by 100 units
top and bottom (ClipToBounds="False" on both grids permits this). Everything inside a bar is
scaled by the same 2/3 so the status/home indicators stay proportional.
================================================================================================

================================================================================================
MASK OVERFLOW — why the two side masks carry huge negative margins.
================================================================================================
This whole mock-up lives in a Viewbox with Stretch="Uniform", so the 1920x1080 grid below is
scaled to FIT its container and centred. Whenever the container is not exactly 16:9 — which is
the normal case for the Granular editor's video pane and the Main App preview — that leaves
pillarbox bars to the left and right (or letterbox bars above and below) of the scaled content.

The masks used to be plain 600-unit columns, so they covered only as far as the scaled grid
reached. The bars beyond it stayed BRIGHT: the centre dimmed correctly and the far left and
right edges suddenly did not, which is exactly the reported symptom. Those outer bars are just
as discarded by the portrait crop as everything else outside the 720-unit slice.

Negative margins let each mask paint far outside the grid without changing the grid's measured
size, so the Viewbox's uniform scale — and therefore every coordinate in this control — is
completely unaffected. The overflow is bounded by the HOST, which clips: the Granular video
Border and the Main App video Grid both set ClipToBounds="True". Do not "tidy" these margins
away, and do not turn clipping back on for the Viewbox.
================================================================================================

### near PortraitImage (line 75)

TEXT STRIP — MAPS 1:1 ONTO THE EXPORTED 150px BAND. DO NOT SHRINK IT.

The exporter overlays the text picture at 0,0 on the 1080x1920 canvas
(MobileFilterBuilder line 157), so it fills the whole 1080x150 top band edge
to edge. TextOverlayGenerator.GeneratePng always produces exactly 1080x150 —
both call sites use the defaults (MainWindow line 2137, ProcessWorker line
290) — and 1080/150 is 7.2, precisely the same shape as this 720x100 bar
(720/100 = 7.2). So filling the bar reproduces the export exactly, with no
distortion. Stretch="Fill" states that intent; because the two shapes match,
it behaves identically to Uniform while making a future size mismatch
obvious instead of silently letterboxing.

WHAT THIS REPLACED: Height="70" with Margin="0,28,0,0". Uniform then forced
the width to 70 x 7.2 = 504 units inside a 720-unit screen, so the preview
showed your text at 70% of its real width and pushed 28% down the band. That
ratio dated back to the original 720x1080 mock-up and survived the later
geometry fix unchanged, so it had never matched the export.

ZIndex: the decorative status bar below is declared after this image and
would otherwise paint over it. The real export has no status bar — the text
is the only thing in that band — so when long text wraps upward and reaches
the chrome, the text must win. That is what actually renders.

## src/FreeVideoStudio.App/Controls/TimelineLanesControl.axaml

### near ColumnDefinitions — LANES_03, ZOOM_01 (line 6)

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SHARED TWO-LANE TIMELINE (LANES_03)

ONE control, used by BOTH the Granular Speed Editor and Music Wizard phase 3. It owns
everything the two windows had been duplicating: the ruler, the gridlines, the caret and
all click-to-seek behaviour. The windows supply only their own lane CONTENT.

col 0 : elapsed clock   (counts UP   — time into the clip)
col 1 : row 0 marker headroom 0px    <- ZOOM_01, height set by MarkerHeadroomPx
row 1 ruler 22px
row 2 LANE A host 60px   <- window fills this
row 3 LANE B host 60px   <- window fills this
overlays spanning rows 1-3: gridlines, seek surfaces, caret
col 2 : remaining clock (counts DOWN — time left)

⚠️ THE SEEK SURFACES ARE PER-ROW, NOT ONE BIG ONE. Granular's upper lane handles its own
pointer input (block drag, edge resize, drag-to-create), so a single surface spanning
everything would swallow it. Each row gets its own, switched on independently.

⚠️ THE CARET GRAB BOX SITS ABOVE THE SEEK SURFACES on purpose — grabbing the playhead must
never register as a click-to-seek. That is the whole reason it has a widened hit area.

ZOOM_01 — HORIZONTAL AFFINE SCALING (viewport virtualization). LanesGrid is sized IN
CODE to viewport-width × ZoomFactor and lives inside a horizontal ScrollViewer that
supplies the pan extent. Every layer stretches to that width, so every `fraction ×
Bounds.Width` computation — this control's ruler, gridlines and caret, and the host
windows' SrcMsToX/XToSrcMs pairs — is zoom-correct with no per-layer scaling code.
⚠️ DO NOT "fix" this with a RenderTransform ScaleTransform instead: a RenderTransform
does not affect layout, so the ScrollViewer would have no extent to scroll, and
combining a transform with zoom-aware pixel math double-scales. The zoom factor enters
through the layer WIDTH, exactly once.
⚠️ THE MARKER HEADROOM ROW IS LOAD-BEARING WHEN ZOOM IS ON. The floating camera markers
paint up to 52px ABOVE the ruler; inside a ScrollViewer that band must be real content
space or the presenter clip deletes the marker heads. The host sets MarkerHeadroomPx
(56 in the Granular editor) and cancels the on-screen growth with a matching negative
top margin so the ruler stays exactly where it was.
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### near HorizontalScrollBarVisibility — ZOOM_01 (line 51)

ZOOM_01 — the horizontal viewport. LanesGrid's width is driven from this viewport in

layer's pixel math share one definition of "how zoomed are we".

### near RowDefinition — ZOOM_01 (line 59)

ZOOM_01 — headroom for the floating markers (see the header note). Height 0
by default so non-zoomed hosts (Music Wizard phase 3) are laid out exactly
as before; MarkerHeadroomPx sets it from code.

### near RulerCanvas (line 69)

Ruler. Explicit Height, NOT MinHeight: a Canvas reports zero desired size, so an

### near GridlinesCanvas (line 91)

Faint vertical gridlines dropping from every ruler tick through both lanes, so a

### near RulerSeekCanvas (line 96)

Per-row seek surfaces (see the header note).

### near MarkerOverlayCanvas — MARKER_01, ZOOM_01 (line 110)

MARKER_01 — FLOATING MARKER LAYER.
For markers that must sit ON TOP OF the timeline rather than inside a lane: a
"popsicle" camera head above the ruler with its stick dropping down through the
lanes, exactly like the thumbnail mark on the Main App's timeline.

⚠️ IT HAS TO LIVE HERE, NOT IN A LANE. Avalonia's ZIndex only orders SIBLINGS, so a
marker parented inside LaneABorder can never rise above the seek surfaces at
ZIndex 100 however high its own ZIndex is — its whole lane sits below them. Drawn
in a lane, a marker had its head swallowed by the ruler's seek surface the instant
it poked up out of that lane. To the user that is not a z-order subtlety, it is a
marker that cannot be grabbed.

150 is deliberate: above both seek surfaces so a marker takes the click, below the
caret at 200 so grabbing the playhead still wins.

NO Background on purpose — an empty Canvas is not hit-testable, so ordinary clicks
fall straight through to the seek surfaces underneath and only real marker children
take input. ClipToBounds=False lets a head float above the ruler INTO THE HEADROOM
ROW (ZOOM_01: inside a ScrollViewer that only works if the headroom row reserves
the space).

### near CaretHost (line 133)

Caret: a wide invisible grab column carrying a thin visible line, plus the time
badge. Spans the ruler and both lanes so all three always agree.

### near WorkAreaGrid — LAYOUT_01, SPLIT_01, ISSUE_02 (line 161)

LAYOUT_01 (F1) — was ColumnDefinitions="*,Auto". The right column hosts a Viewbox
wrapping a fixed <Grid Width="1920" Height="1280"> composer. A Viewbox measures its
child with INFINITE available size, so under an Auto column it reported a desired
width of 1920px; together with the LAYERS panel (MinWidth 180) and the undo/redo
column the right side demanded ~2200px before the star column got a single pixel.
On any normal display the left column — video, frozen frame, timeline and every
primary button — collapsed to zero width, which is why this screen showed nothing.
Star sizing gives each side a real share and lets the Viewbox scale down to
whatever it is given. Do not restore Auto here.

SPLIT_01 — 65/35, not 50/50. The landscape frame is where the pixel-accurate work
happens: the user is placing a box around a HUD element a few dozen pixels across,
on a 1920- or 3840-wide capture. The portrait composer only has to be big enough to
judge a layout. The old Python tool made the same call and used exactly this ratio
(ui_setup.py: main_layout.addWidget(left_pane, 1176) / addWidget(right_pane, 624)).
Now 58/42: the landscape gave some back once its zoom controls became a vertical
strip and its wizard header moved into the profile bar, and the composer is the half
that has to show a 9:16 shape - it is height-limited, so every point of width it
gains is width it can actually use.
ISSUE_02 (audit round 6): named so SetProfileGate can switch the WHOLE working area
off while the profile gate is up. The gate used to be a hit-test blocker only, which
stops the mouse and nothing else: PortraitCanvas is visible, Focusable and a tab stop
from the moment the window opens, and SetProfileGate never disabled it, so Tab walked
straight through the lock into the canvas the lock exists to protect. The gate
overlay is a SIBLING of this grid (declared after it, ZIndex 9000), so disabling this
grid never disables the gate itself.

### near SnapshotScroll — ZOOM_01, ZOOMBAR_01 (line 250)

ZOOM_01 - the frozen frame is a FIXED-PIXEL surface. LoadSnapshotAsync
writes the real capture size (1920x1080, 2560x1440, ...) onto
SnapshotImage and SourceCanvas, so GetPosition(SourceCanvas) returns true
SOURCE pixels and the rubber band needs no scaling maths of its own.
The zoom is a LayoutTransformControl, NOT a Viewbox and NOT a resize of
the canvas: a LayoutTransform scales the rendered surface while Avalonia
keeps transforming pointer positions back into the canvas's own 1:1
space, so every existing coordinate call site keeps working untouched.
A Viewbox would always fit and could never allow 100% or zoom-in.
The controls that drive it live in ZoomStrip (ZOOMBAR_01).

Stretch="Fill": SnapshotImage is given its exact capture size in
code, so Fill is an identity draw. Uniform would silently
letterbox a non-16:9 capture and break the 1:1 mapping the
selection maths depends on.

### near RolePopupScrim — ROLEPOPUP_01, SLIDER_09, ISSUE_09, POPUPCLEAR_01, ISSUE_08 (line 286)

ROLEPOPUP_01 - the HUD element chooser.
A sibling of the ScrollViewer IN THE SAME GRID CELL, declared AFTER it so
it paints on top (declaration order is the mechanism among siblings -
04_UI_UX_AVALONIA_SPEC.md#UI-THEME, SLIDER_09). It is deliberately NOT an
Avalonia Popup or Flyout: those are separate OS windows, which is how the
old Python RoleToolbar earned its multi-monitor bug and its
"_get_ideal_popup_rect" screen-clamping code. An in-panel Border cannot
leave the window, so none of that is needed.
Alignment is Left/Top with the Margin written from code, because the
position has to track a selection that lives on a zoomed, scrolled canvas
(see PositionRolePopup).
ISSUE_09 (audit round 6): the BoxShadow attribute that used to sit on this
Border carried a raw literal (`0 4 18 0 #66000000`) - the only hardcoded
colour left in this file, and a fixed 40%-black smear that did not change
with the Light/Dark ThemeDictionaries every other colour here follows.
BoxShadows cannot take a per-stop DynamicResource, so the shadow is now
built in code from the themed `AppPopupShadowColor` token and rebuilt on
ActualThemeVariantChanged. See ApplyRolePopupShadow().
POPUPCLEAR_01 - MaxWidth/MaxHeight are a hard ceiling so the "does it
fit?" test in PositionRolePopup is answerable. A profile with many
elements would otherwise grow the popup past the panel, no placement
would fit, and every position would fall through to the last-resort
branch. The inner ScrollViewer is what lets a long list live inside
that ceiling instead of bursting it.
ISSUE_08 (audit round 6): the lightbox behind the chooser.
RolePopup is an in-panel Border rather than a Popup/Flyout on purpose
(ROLEPOPUP_01), which is right - but it meant the chooser had no dimming
and, not being a Popup, no IsLightDismissEnabled either. It floated over
a fully lit, fully clickable frame, so it did not read as a question that
has to be answered, and there was no click-away path at all (Escape was
the only exit). This scrim supplies both: it dims the frame underneath and
it swallows the click that dismisses. Declared BEFORE RolePopup so the
popup still paints on top of it (declaration order is the mechanism among
siblings - 04_UI_UX_AVALONIA_SPEC.md#UI-THEME, SLIDER_09).

obtained via GetPosition(PortraitCanvas) are automatically

the composer's width — in a side-by-side panel that is roughly 340px,
and the user cannot judge a HUD layout at that size. The bezel was
costing 62% of the width to say something the 9:16 shape already says.

QGraphicsView on a 1080x1920 scene, fitted to the panel.
PhoneFrameMockup is untouched and still used elsewhere in the suite.

ISSUE_5 still holds and is why this is a Viewbox over a FIXED-SIZE grid:
the composer works in absolute portrait pixels, so item coordinates, the
background reference and the letterbox stay in exact 1:1 alignment at any
window size or DPI, and GetPosition(PortraitCanvas) returns true
1080x1920 pixels because Avalonia inverts the Viewbox transform for us.

### near WandOverlay — WANDPROGRESS_01 (line 870)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
WANDPROGRESS_01 — WHAT THE MAGIC WAND IS DOING, WHILE IT DOES IT.
The wand can run for anything from three seconds to its sixty-second ceiling, and
until now the ONLY thing that changed on screen was the button going grey and
reading "ANALYSING…". From outside, a long job and a hung one look identical, so
the user is left deciding for themselves whether the feature works — and a feature
you have to guess about is a feature people stop pressing.
This says the three things that settle it: a bar that moves, a percentage, and a
sentence naming what is being looked at right now. Plus a way out: the wand is
optional, and a user who has changed their mind should not have to wait for it.
Modal on purpose (ZIndex above the gate, tab cycle, hit-test on): the frozen frame
must not be edited underneath a detector that is about to draw boxes on it.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### near Win32 — AOTSAFETY_03, AOTCLEAN_02, AOTCLEAN_01 (line 24)

AOTSAFETY_03: Avalonia.Controls.ColorPicker and Avalonia.Controls.DataGrid were removed.
Neither is used by any .cs or .axaml file in src\. DataGrid was rooted with
TrimmerRootAssembly, which forced whole-assembly analysis and emitted the IL2104/IL3053
lines that failed the release build.
AOTCLEAN_02: NAudio.Core + NAudio.WinMM only (WaveOutEvent / WaveInEvent / WAV I/O).
The NAudio umbrella package pulled NAudio.Wasapi (MediaFoundation over classic COM
interop, which NativeAOT cannot run: IL2050), Asio, Midi and WinForms into the binary.
Its only type we used, AudioFileReader, is replaced by Core\Media\WavAudioReader.cs.
AOTCLEAN_01: SkiaSharp 3 overrides, the documented way to run Avalonia 11.3.6+ on SkiaSharp 3
(2.88's SKObject.PtrToStructure<T> was IL2091). Managed and every native asset MUST move
together: a 2.88 native library under the 3.x managed layer throws at the first bitmap.

### near ItemGroup — AOTCLEAN_03 (line 43)

AOTCLEAN_03: Vortice.Direct3D11 / Vortice.DXGI removed. They brought SharpGen.Runtime,
whose reflection-based vtable registry is not trim-safe (IL2067/IL2072). The preview's
handful of D3D11/DXGI calls are now direct vtable calls in Interop\D3D11Interop.cs.

### near click — AUDIO_08 (line 48)

AUDIO_08: the six UI sound effects used to live as base64 STRING LITERALS inside
UiSoundEffect.cs (663,680 base64 chars for 497,758 bytes of PCM). .NET stores string
literals as UTF-16 in the assembly's #US heap, so that cost ~1.27 MB of binary to carry
~486 KB of audio, plus a second full copy decoded onto the managed heap at startup — in an
app whose #2 mandate is a single condensed .exe. They are now real .wav files embedded as
resources (raw bytes, no 2x encoding penalty, loaded lazily on first use).
LogicalName is set EXPLICITLY so the lookup can never break from a RootNamespace or folder
rename. These are deliberately NOT LFS-tracked (unlike *.mp3/*.mp4 in .gitattributes):
they are build-critical inputs, and an LFS pointer file in a clone without LFS would embed
130 bytes of text as a "sound" and fail silently. 486 KB of plain git blob is cheaper than
that failure mode.

### near TrimmerRootAssembly — NODROPPER_01 (line 68)

NODROPPER_01 — payload.zip is NOT embedded any more. The program used to carry FFmpeg, libmpv,
the starter media and a copy of itself as a compressed managed resource and unpack them on first
run: the dropper pattern antivirus engines flag. The release is packed by Inno Setup instead
(build\installer\FreeVideoStudio.iss). Do not add an EmbeddedResource for any executable payload.

### near DEPENDENTLOADFLAG — WORKERSTAGE_01 (line 78)

WORKERSTAGE_01: the program's STATIC imports resolve from System32 only (DependentLoadFlags =
LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_SYSTEM32). Every DLL it imports statically is a Windows system DLL; the app's
own native libraries (Skia, HarfBuzz, ANGLE, libmpv, FFmpeg) are loaded at run time by full path,
which this flag does not affect. A DLL dropped beside the program can therefore never be loaded
as one of its imports - which matters most for the elevated update worker.

### near CopyDevBinaries (line 92)

DEV ONLY: Copy native binaries (mpv, ffmpeg) to the output folder after every
Debug build so the app can run locally via `dotnet run` or `dotnet watch run`.
Does NOT affect production NativeAOT publish (Release).

### near SuppressTrimAnalysisWarnings — AOTSAFETY_01 (line 122)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
AOTSAFETY_01 — THE TRIM AND AOT ANALYSERS ARE ON. DO NOT SET THESE BACK TO true.
These two properties used to be true, which did not make the app AOT-safe; it made the app
SILENT about not being AOT-safe. A trim warning is the compiler predicting "this reflection
call has no metadata left after trimming and will throw at run time". Suppressed, the
prediction still comes true — it just arrives as a NotSupportedException on a user's
machine, in the published single .exe only, where it cannot be reproduced from a Debug run.
Mandate #1 makes that one .exe the entire product, so the analyser that guards it may not
be muted.
Warnings here are WARNINGS, not errors: the build still succeeds. Each one is either fixed
(usually by moving to a source-generated JsonSerializerContext, as Ipc/IpcProtocol.cs
already does) or explicitly annotated at the call site with a comment saying why it is
provably safe. Silencing the whole category to clear the build log is how this got here.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### near assets — AOTSAFETY_01 (line 138)

AOTSAFETY_01: IlcTrimMetadata stays false. It is a SIZE/behaviour switch that keeps
metadata the app needs at run time, not an analyser mute, and turning it on would change
what the shipped binary can do. Unrelated to the two properties above.

### near CS1998 — AOTSAFETY_01 (line 144)

AOTSAFETY_01: IL2104 ("assembly produced trim warnings") removed from NoWarn. It is the
summary line that names which assembly is unsafe; muting it while re-enabling the detailed
warnings would hide the headline and keep the noise. CS1998/CS0414 are unrelated style
warnings and stay suppressed.

### near AllowUnsafeBlocks — AOTCLEAN_01 (line 149)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
AOTCLEAN_01 — ZERO TRIM/AOT WARNINGS, NOTHING MUTED, NOTHING COLLAPSED.
Build.cmd publishes with TreatWarningsAsErrors=true and every IL2xxx/IL3xxx code is fatal,
first-party AND third-party. The 2026-09-25 interim (IL2104/IL3053 made non-fatal, third-
party detail collapsed with TrimmerSingleWarn, IL2026 muted at the ILC stage) is gone.
Each finding was fixed at its source instead: see docs/06 §10 PROJ-AOTPOLICY.
AotSafetyRuleTests fails the build if a mute, a collapse or a WarningsNotAsErrors entry
for any IL code comes back.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### near PropertyGroup — ISSUE_03, PEIDENTITY_01 (line 162)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ISSUE_03 — WIN32 BINARY IDENTITY. DO NOT DELETE THESE, AND DO NOT LEAVE THEM BLANK.
Until this block existed the shipped single .exe carried .NET's silent defaults: FileVersion
1.0.0.0, no Company, no Product, no Copyright. Right-click > Properties > Details was empty,
which is what a user checks when SmartScreen stops an unknown download — so the one place
they went looking for reassurance said nothing at all. Mandate #2 makes this ONE file the
entire product; it has to be able to introduce itself.
⚠️ Product metadata carries ONLY the "Free Video Studio" brand. Game names are third-party
trademarks and this string is embedded in a binary that is distributed publicly. See
docs/REBRAND_MIGRATION.md for the complete brand identity.
⚠️ PEIDENTITY_01 — NativeAOT copies the version resource from the managed assembly, so
OriginalFilename / InternalName come out as "FreeVideoStudio.dll". FvsBuild (PeIdentity.cs)
rewrites both to "FreeVideoStudio.exe" before signing; a binary naming another file is the
renamed-binary pattern antivirus scores. app.manifest's version is synchronized too.
⚠️ Bump <Version> on every release. AssemblyVersion is pinned to a 1.0.0.0-style major line on
purpose so assembly binding never breaks between patch releases; FileVersion and
InformationalVersion carry the real number that users and bug reports see.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### near DeleteSegmentBtn — ISSUE_01, ZOOM_04 (line 601)

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
⚠️⚠️ ISSUE_01 — THESE TWO PROMPTS USED TO BE PURE DECORATION. ⚠️⚠️
A Button that owns a Flyout opens that Flyout by itself AND still raises
Click. Both buttons had a Click handler that destroyed the work outright,
so the sequence a user actually experienced was: segments gone -> "are you
sure?" -> a CONFIRM button wired to nothing at all. There is no undo in
this window.
THE RULE NOW (identical to Merger RemoveVideoButton and CropTool RESET):
the Click handler acts ONLY when the user has switched the confirmation
OFF in Settings > Confirmation Dialogs. Otherwise it does nothing and the
flyout asks; the CONFIRM button is the ONLY path that destroys anything.
⚠️ NEVER put destructive work back into the outer button's Click handler.
The dialog is also deliberately LARGE (MinWidth 380, 48px buttons, plain
English, an explicit KEEP escape) — the old 8px-margin strip was easy to
click straight through without reading.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ZOOM_04: the ONLY way to change a zoom. ZOOM-IN refuses to reopen a block
that already has one (owner's decision — a mis-drag on re-entry would
silently overwrite coordinates that were already right), so editing is
deliberately remove-then-redo. Visible only when the selected block
actually carries a zoom.

MEME_07: THE REBUILD STALL. Adding, moving or removing a meme changes the finished
video's length and every frame position after the meme, so the output ruler, the film
strip and the preview all have to be rebuilt before the timeline can be scrubbed
truthfully. That takes a moment. This blocks the WHOLE window while it happens, on
purpose: a half-rebuilt timeline that still accepts clicks is how a user ends up
dragging a marker onto a position that no longer exists. It cannot be missed and it
cannot be clicked through.

### near MenuShowShortcuts — ISSUE_05 (line 55)

ISSUE_05: the "?" key alone was not a discoverable way in, and on keyboard
layouts where ? is not on the OemQuestion key it does not fire at all.
This menu item is the guaranteed route. Do not remove it in favour of the
shortcut.
⚠️ NO `InputGesture` HERE, EVER. Avalonia parses that attribute with
`KeyGesture.Parse`, which resolves the key name through `Enum.Parse<Key>`.
"?" is not a member of the Key enum, so `InputGesture="?"` throws
`ArgumentException: Requested value '?' was not found.` at XAML load —
AFTER a clean build, so it presents as the app exiting with code 1 on
startup rather than as a compile error. The hint lives in the header
text instead. If you ever do want a real gesture here it must be a
parseable name such as "OemQuestion" or "Ctrl+K".

video anywhere on screen; the video only appeared on step 3, and changing the start meant

heard against the picture straight away.

### near Right — SLIDER_01, SLIDER_02, SLIDER_03, SLIDER_05, LAYOUT_02, AUDIO_09, LAYOUT_03, SLIDER_06 (line 315)

SLIDER_01 - ZIndex MUST STAY ABOVE THE LANES ROW.
The knobs grow to scale(2.0) while held: a 44px thumb RENDERS 88px and
overflows by 22px in every direction. This row was ZIndex="5" while the
lanes Grid above it is ZIndex="10", so the lanes painted over the overflow
and the knob looked sliced off. Do not lower it below the lanes row.

SLIDER_02 - both sliders live in one framed "MIX LEVELS" card. The frame's
horizontal Padding is what stops the knob being clipped at 0% and 100%: the
dot centre sits 22px inside the slider, and at scale(2.0) the 52px dot reaches
4px PAST the slider edge, so it needs real clearance to paint into. Do not
reduce that padding below ~16.

SLIDER_03 - they sit SIDE BY SIDE inside that card, not stacked. See the note
on the inner Grid: this screen is short of vertical space and has horizontal
space to spare.
SLIDER_01 - ZIndex MUST STAY ABOVE THE LANES ROW.
The knobs grow to scale(2.0) while held and overflow their row vertically.
This was ZIndex="5" while the lanes Grid above is ZIndex="10", so the lanes
painted over the overflow and the knob looked sliced off at the top.

SLIDER_05 - ONE ROW, NOT THREE. This screen is the tightest in the suite for
vertical space (video preview + ruler + two 60px lanes + transport + nav all
compete), so MIX LEVELS is now a SINGLE row: the frame caption sits inline on
the left and each label sits inline beside its own slider. That removed the
separate caption row and the separate label row - roughly 45px back.
The labels are also short ("Video 100%" not "Video Volume: 100%") so they steal
as little width as possible from the sliders.
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
LAYOUT_02 — THE MIX LEVELS ROW IS GONE. THE SLIDERS ARE NOW VERTICAL,
IN A COLUMN TO THE RIGHT OF THE WHOLE PHASE.

Phase 3 is starved of HEIGHT and has plenty of WIDTH. Two horizontal
sliders in a framed card cost a full bottom row (~60px) purely to move
two values that only need one dimension. Rotated 270 degrees they cost
~90px of width — which was going spare — and give that height back to
the video, the only elastic row in the panel.

⚠️ THE SLIDERS ARE THE SAME CONTROLS WITH THE SAME NAMES. VideoVolSlider
and MusicVolSlider are still found by FindControl, still 0-100, still
wired to the same handlers. ONLY the orientation and position changed.
⚠️ ClipToBounds="False" IS LOAD-BEARING (SLIDER_02/04). The 52px thumb
paints outside its own track at 0% and 100%; a clipping parent shears the
knob off at the extremes. Do not "tidy" it away.
⚠️ The ducking toggle that used to sit beside these is now in Settings —
see AUDIO_09.
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
LAYOUT_03 — ANCHORED TO THE VIDEO BOX, TOP AND BOTTOM.

This was Grid.Row="0" Grid.RowSpan="4": it started level with
the CONFIRM MUSIC heading (visibly taller than the picture it
sits beside) and ran down through the lanes row, pushing the
timeline off the right-hand side of the window.

It is now Grid.Row="1" ONLY — the video preview's own row — so
VerticalAlignment="Stretch" makes its top and bottom edges land
exactly on the top and bottom of VideoHostBorder. The bottom
margin matches that row's own Margin="0,0,0,10" so the two
boxes end on the same line rather than the slider frame hanging
10px lower.

⚠️ Do NOT restore a RowSpan here. The lanes row now spans both
columns (LAYOUT_03) and would render underneath this panel.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SLIDER_06 — TWO TRAYS IN ONE RACK, AND NARROW.

The two faders shared a single open panel with 14px of air
between them and nothing to say where one channel ended and the
next began. Each now sits in its OWN inset compartment — a
darker AppSurfaceBrush well inside the lighter AppPanelBrush
rack — so the pair still reads as one MIX control while each
channel is unmistakably its own slot.

WIDTH. This column is pure overhead: every pixel it takes comes
off the video preview beside it (LAYOUT_02). The old width was
driven by the LABELS, not the sliders — "Video 100%" measures
wider than the 44px fader it sat under, so the text set the
column width and the fader wasted the rest. Split in two, the
channel name moves to a caption ABOVE the fader and the value
below is just the number, so nothing in the tray is wider than
the fader itself. With the gap at 5px and the rack padding at
5px the whole rack is roughly a quarter narrower than before.

⚠️ ClipToBounds="False" IS STILL LOAD-BEARING, on the trays as
well as the rack (SLIDER_02/04). The thumb grows to scale(2.0)
while held and paints outside its own track; a clipping tray
would shear the knob off at the sides. Do not "tidy" it away,
and do not give the trays ClipToBounds="True" to stop the
overflow — the overflow is the press feedback.

The knob grows past the ends of its own track at 0% and

high ZIndex on the Slider did NOT lift it above them: it
stayed declared BETWEEN the two TextBlocks, and the one
after it kept painting over the overflow.
The reliable rule among siblings of one panel is the
order they are WRITTEN, so the Slider is now the LAST
child of this Grid while keeping Grid.Row="1" — its
LAYOUT slot is unchanged, only its place in the paint
sequence moved. ZIndex stays as agreement, not as the
mechanism.

layout slots are real rectangles that would otherwise
swallow a press aimed at the knob where it overlaps them.

TextBlock re-breaks this, silently and invisibly in code.

SLIDER_07: NO Width, NO MinWidth. A vertical Slider must be
left to size itself to its own track — anything wider puts
the rail against one edge and slices the knob in half (the
fault this replaced). CompactSlider is the suite's narrow
thumb and its own note names vertical volume as its case.

height for three things that are each one line tall. The row
below is 50px and carries all of it:

[● REC]  [MIC]  [PAUSE]  [═══ EQ ═══]  [PLAY]  [● READY]

The two lamps mean DIFFERENT things and that is the point:
RecordingLight (left, red)  — lit ONLY while capture is live.
ReadyLamp      (right, green) — lit when a microphone is
present and the preview is up.
VOREC_01 — the left lamp is a SHAPE as well as a colour (dot =
live, ring = starting/saving, two bars = paused, triangle =
failed, tick = saved) and RecordingBadgeText says it in words
with the CAPTURED-audio time ("REC 0:07.3"). Both, plus the
status word on the right, are written by ONE method:
VoiceOverWindow.RefreshRecordingIndicator.
⚠️ Avalonia Grid has NO ColumnSpacing (that is WinUI/WPF and it
fails the WHOLE file with AVLN:0004). Gaps are Margins.

### near RecordPauseButton (line 119)

Pause / Resume for an in-progress take.
Hidden until recording starts (code-behind drives IsVisible).
Pausing CLOSES the current take and resuming opens a new one that
re-anchors itself to the video clock, so pausing as often as you
like cannot push the voiceover out of sync.

### near AppMeterBackgroundBrush — SPECTRUM_03, SPECTRUM_04 (line 135)

SPECTRUM_03 / SPECTRUM_04 — the microphone's REAL frequency spectrum,
live from the moment a microphone is selected, not only while
recording. One narrow bar per band, 60 Hz (left) to 16 kHz
(right); height = band level (-60..0 dBFS); green / amber / red =
level zone. 68px tall (was a 34px strip): the bars need the height
to be legible, and the transport buttons are 50px so the row grows
by 18px out of the video's star row, not out of the timeline.

### near RowDefinitions — VOTL_01 (line 164)

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
VOTL_01 — THE TIMELINE STACK.

Row 0  clock strip   elapsed / total / remaining, same
wording and format as the main screen.
Row 1  ruler         ticks + labels + the big playhead caret.
Row 2  film lane     60px, and where TAKES now live.
Row 3  game audio    60px.

All four rows are FULL WIDTH and share one X axis. That is not
cosmetic: the caret and all three playhead lines are positioned
from the same `fraction`, so insetting any one row (e.g. putting
the clock labels beside the ruler) would silently desynchronise
the caret from the lanes. The clock therefore gets its own row.

### near LiveRecordingCanvas — VOREC_03, SLIDER_09 (line 205)

⚠️ VOREC_03 / SLIDER_09 — DECLARATION ORDER IS THE PAINT ORDER. The take canvas
and the live recording canvas are declared AFTER ThumbLoadingOverlay so that a
take (and above all the take being recorded) is drawn ON TOP of the "Generating
Frames..." scrim instead of being hidden by it while frames are still loading.
The overlay is IsHitTestVisible="False", so the take blocks stay clickable.
Do not "tidy" these back above the overlay.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

it only ever covered the GAME bus — music added in the wizard was
